7213.label: 1 Samuel 1:1
7213.text: Now there happened to be a certain man of Ra·math·aʹim-zoʹphim of the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, and his name was El·kaʹnah, the son of Je·roʹham, the son of E·liʹhu, the son of Toʹhu, the son of Zuph, an Eʹphra·im·ite.

7214.label: 1 Samuel 1:2
7214.text: And he had two wives, the name of the one being Hanʹnah, and the name of the other being Pe·ninʹnah. And Pe·ninʹnah came to have children, but Hanʹnah had no children.

7215.label: 1 Samuel 1:3
7215.text: And that man went up out of his city from year to year to prostrate himself and to sacrifice to Jehovah of armies in Shiʹloh. And there is where the two sons of Eʹli, Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has, were priests to Jehovah.

7216.label: 1 Samuel 1:4
7216.text: And there came to be a day when El·kaʹnah proceeded to sacrifice, and he gave to Pe·ninʹnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions;

7217.label: 1 Samuel 1:5
7217.text: but to Hanʹnah he gave one portion. Nonetheless it was Hanʹnah that he loved, and, as for Jehovah, he had closed up her womb.

7218.label: 1 Samuel 1:6
7218.text: And her rival wife also vexed her sorely for the sake of making her feel disconcerted because Jehovah had closed up her womb.

7219.label: 1 Samuel 1:7
7219.text: And that was the way she would do year by year, as often as she went up into the house of Jehovah. That was the way she would vex her, so that she would weep and not eat.

7220.label: 1 Samuel 1:8
7220.text: And El·kaʹnah her husband proceeded to say to her: “Hanʹnah, why do you weep, and why do you not eat, and why does your heart feel bad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

7221.label: 1 Samuel 1:9
7221.text: Then Hanʹnah got up after they had eaten in Shiʹloh and after the drinking, while Eʹli the priest was sitting upon the seat by the doorpost of the temple of Jehovah.

7222.label: 1 Samuel 1:10
7222.text: And she was bitter of soul, and she began to pray to Jehovah and to weep greatly.

7223.label: 1 Samuel 1:11
7223.text: And she went on to make a vow and say: “O Jehovah of armies, if you will without fail look upon the affliction of your slave girl and actually remember me, and you will not forget your slave girl and actually give to your slave girl a male offspring, I will give him to Jehovah all the days of his life, and no razor will come upon his head.”

7224.label: 1 Samuel 1:12
7224.text: And it occurred that while she prayed extendedly before Jehovah, Eʹli was watching her mouth.

7225.label: 1 Samuel 1:13
7225.text: As for Hanʹnah, she was speaking in her heart; only her lips were quivering, and her voice was not heard. But Eʹli took her for drunk.

7226.label: 1 Samuel 1:14
7226.text: So Eʹli said to her: “How long will you behave drunk? Put away your wine from upon you.”

7227.label: 1 Samuel 1:15
7227.text: At this Hanʹnah answered and said: “No, my lord! A woman hard pressed in spirit I am; and wine and intoxicating liquor I have not drunk, but I pour out my soul before Jehovah.

7228.label: 1 Samuel 1:16
7228.text: Do not make your slave girl like a good-for-nothing woman, for it is out of the abundance of my concern and my vexation that I have spoken until now.”

7229.label: 1 Samuel 1:17
7229.text: Then Eʹli answered and said: “Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”

7230.label: 1 Samuel 1:18
7230.text: To this she said: “Let your maidservant find favor in your eyes.” And the woman proceeded to go on her way and to eat, and her face became self-concerned no more.

7231.label: 1 Samuel 1:19
7231.text: Then they got up early in the morning and prostrated themselves before Jehovah, after which they returned and came into their house at Raʹmah. El·kaʹnah now had intercourse with Hanʹnah his wife, and Jehovah began remembering her.

7232.label: 1 Samuel 1:20
7232.text: So it came about at the rolling around of a year that Hanʹnah became pregnant and brought a son to birth and proceeded to call his name Samuel, because, said she, “it is from Jehovah that I have asked him.”

7233.label: 1 Samuel 1:21
7233.text: In time the man El·kaʹnah went up with all his household to sacrifice to Jehovah the yearly sacrifice and his vow offering.

7234.label: 1 Samuel 1:22
7234.text: As for Hanʹnah, she did not go up, for she had said to her husband: “As soon as the boy is weaned, I must bring him, and he must appear before Jehovah and dwell there to time indefinite.”

7235.label: 1 Samuel 1:23
7235.text: At this El·kaʹnah her husband said to her: “Do what is good in your eyes. Stay at home until you wean him. Only may Jehovah carry out his word.” So the woman stayed at home and kept nursing her son until she weaned him.

7236.label: 1 Samuel 1:24
7236.text: Accordingly just as soon as she had weaned him, she brought him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull and one eʹphah of flour and a large jar of wine, and she proceeded to enter the house of Jehovah in Shiʹloh. And the boy was with her.

7237.label: 1 Samuel 1:25
7237.text: Then they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eʹli.

7238.label: 1 Samuel 1:26
7238.text: With that she said: “Excuse me, my lord! By the life of your soul, my lord, I am the woman that was standing with you in this place to pray to Jehovah.

7239.label: 1 Samuel 1:27
7239.text: It was with reference to this boy that I prayed that Jehovah should grant me my petition that I asked of him.

7240.label: 1 Samuel 1:28
7240.text: And I, in my turn, have lent him to Jehovah. All the days that he does happen to be, he is one requested for Jehovah.” And he proceeded to bow down there to Jehovah.

7241.label: 1 Samuel 2:1
7241.text: And Hanʹnah went on to pray and say:“My heart does exult in Jehovah, My horn is indeed exalted in Jehovah. My mouth is widened against my enemies,For I do rejoice in the salvation from you.

7242.label: 1 Samuel 2:2
7242.text: There is no one holy like Jehovah, for there is no one but you; And there is no rock like our God.

7243.label: 1 Samuel 2:3
7243.text: Do not YOU people speak very haughtily so much,Let nothing go forth unrestrained from YOUR mouth, For a God of knowledge Jehovah is, And by him deeds are rightly estimated.

7244.label: 1 Samuel 2:4
7244.text: The mighty men of the bow are filled with terror, But those that are stumbling do gird on vital energy.

7245.label: 1 Samuel 2:5
7245.text: The satisfied must hire themselves out for bread, But the hungry actually cease [to hunger]. Even the barren has given birth to seven, But she that was abundant in sons has faded away.

7246.label: 1 Samuel 2:6
7246.text: Jehovah is a Killer and a Preserver of life, A Bringer down to Sheʹol, and He brings up.

7247.label: 1 Samuel 2:7
7247.text: Jehovah is an Impoverisher and an Enricher, An Abaser, also an Exalter,

7248.label: 1 Samuel 2:8
7248.text: A Raiser of a lowly one from the dust; From the ashpit he lifts up a poor one, To make them sit with nobles; and a throne of glory he gives to them as a possession. For to Jehovah belong earth’s supports, And he places upon them the productive land.

7249.label: 1 Samuel 2:9
7249.text: The feet of his loyal ones he guards; As for the wicked ones, they are silenced in darkness, For not by power does a man prove superior.

7250.label: 1 Samuel 2:10
7250.text: As for Jehovah, those contending against him will be terrified; Against them he will thunder in the heavens. Jehovah himself will judge the ends of the earth, That he may give strength to his king, That he may exalt the horn of his anointed one.”

7251.label: 1 Samuel 2:11
7251.text: Then El·kaʹnah went to Raʹmah to his house; and as for the boy, he became a minister of Jehovah before Eʹli the priest.

7252.label: 1 Samuel 2:12
7252.text: Now the sons of Eʹli were good-for-nothing men; they did not acknowledge Jehovah.

7253.label: 1 Samuel 2:13
7253.text: As for the due right of the priests from the people, whenever any man was offering a sacrifice, an attendant of the priest came with the three-pronged fork in his hand, just when the meat was boiling,

7254.label: 1 Samuel 2:14
7254.text: and made a thrust into the basin or the two-handled cooking pot or the caldron or the one-handled cooking pot. Anything that the fork might bring up the priest would take for himself. That is the way they would do in Shiʹloh to all the Israelites coming there.

7255.label: 1 Samuel 2:15
7255.text: Also, before ever they could make the fat smoke, an attendant of the priest came and said to the man sacrificing: “Do give meat to roast for the priest so that he may receive from you, not boiled meat, but raw.”

7256.label: 1 Samuel 2:16
7256.text: When the man would say to him: “Let them be sure to make the fat smoke first of all. Then take for yourself just whatever your soul may crave,” he actually said: “No, but you should give it now; and, if not, I shall have to take it by force!”

7257.label: 1 Samuel 2:17
7257.text: And the sin of the attendants came to be very great before Jehovah; for the men treated the offering of Jehovah with disrespect.

7258.label: 1 Samuel 2:18
7258.text: And Samuel was ministering before Jehovah, as a boy, having a linen ephʹod girded on.

7259.label: 1 Samuel 2:19
7259.text: Also, a little sleeveless coat his mother would make for him, and she brought it up to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to sacrifice the yearly sacrifice.

7260.label: 1 Samuel 2:20
7260.text: And Eʹli blessed El·kaʹnah and his wife and said: “May Jehovah appoint to you an offspring from this wife in place of the thing lent, that was lent to Jehovah.” And they went to their place.

7261.label: 1 Samuel 2:21
7261.text: Accordingly Jehovah turned his attention to Hanʹnah, so that she had pregnancy and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel continued growing up with Jehovah.

7262.label: 1 Samuel 2:22
7262.text: And Eʹli was very old, and he had heard of all that his sons kept doing to all Israel and how they would lie down with the women that were serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

7263.label: 1 Samuel 2:23
7263.text: And he used to say to them: “Why do YOU keep doing things like these? For the things I am hearing about YOU from all the people are bad.

7264.label: 1 Samuel 2:24
7264.text: No, my sons, because the report is not good that I am hearing, that the people of Jehovah are causing to circulate.

7265.label: 1 Samuel 2:25
7265.text: If a man should sin against a man, God will arbitrate for him; but if it is against Jehovah that a man should sin, who is there to pray for him?” But they would not listen to the voice of their father, because Jehovah was now pleased to put them to death.

7266.label: 1 Samuel 2:26
7266.text: All the while the boy Samuel was growing bigger and more likable both from Jehovah’s standpoint and from that of men.

7267.label: 1 Samuel 2:27
7267.text: And a man of God proceeded to come to Eʹli and say to him: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘Did I not for a fact reveal myself to the house of your forefather while they happened to be in Egypt as slaves to the house of Pharʹaoh?

7268.label: 1 Samuel 2:28
7268.text: And there was a choosing of him out of all the tribes of Israel for me, to act as priest and go up upon my altar to make sacrificial smoke billow up, to bear an ephʹod before me, that I might give to the house of your forefather all the offerings made by fire of the sons of Israel.

7269.label: 1 Samuel 2:29
7269.text: Why do YOU men keep kicking at my sacrifice and at my offering that I have commanded [in my] dwelling, and you keep honoring your sons more than me by fattening yourselves from the best of every offering of Israel my people?

7270.label: 1 Samuel 2:30
7270.text: “‘That is why the utterance of Jehovah the God of Israel is: “I did indeed say, As for your house and the house of your forefather, they will walk before me to time indefinite.” But now the utterance of Jehovah is: “It is unthinkable, on my part, because those honoring me I shall honor, and those despising me will be of little account.”

7271.label: 1 Samuel 2:31
7271.text: Look! Days are coming when I shall certainly chop off your arm and the arm of the house of your forefather, so that there will not come to be an old man in your house.

7272.label: 1 Samuel 2:32
7272.text: And you will actually look upon an adversary [in my] dwelling amid all the good that is done to Israel; and never will there come to be an old man in your house.

7273.label: 1 Samuel 2:33
7273.text: And yet there is a man of yours that I shall not cut off from being at my altar so as to cause your eyes to fail and to make your soul pine away; but the greater number of your house will all die by the sword of men.

7274.label: 1 Samuel 2:34
7274.text: And this is the sign for you that will come to your two sons, Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has: On one day both of them will die.

7275.label: 1 Samuel 2:35
7275.text: And I shall certainly raise up for myself a faithful priest. In harmony with what is in my heart and in my soul he will do; and I shall certainly build for him a lasting house, and he will certainly walk before my anointed one always.

7276.label: 1 Samuel 2:36
7276.text: And it must occur that anyone left over in your house will come and bow down to him for the payment of money and a round loaf of bread, and will certainly say: “Attach me, please, to one of the priestly offices to eat a piece of bread.”’”

7277.label: 1 Samuel 3:1
7277.text: All the while the boy Samuel was ministering to Jehovah before Eʹli, and word from Jehovah had become rare in those days; there was no vision being spread abroad.

7278.label: 1 Samuel 3:2
7278.text: Now it came about on that day that Eʹli was lying in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow dim; he was not able to see.

7279.label: 1 Samuel 3:3
7279.text: And the lamp of God was not yet extinguished, and Samuel was lying in the temple of Jehovah, where the ark of God was.

7280.label: 1 Samuel 3:4
7280.text: And Jehovah proceeded to call Samuel. At this he said: “Here I am.”

7281.label: 1 Samuel 3:5
7281.text: And he went running to Eʹli and saying: “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said: “I did not call. Lie down again.” So he went and lay down.

7282.label: 1 Samuel 3:6
7282.text: And Jehovah went on to call yet again: “Samuel!” At this Samuel got up and went to Eʹli and said: “Here I am, for you did call me.” But he said: “I did not call, my son. Lie down again.”

7283.label: 1 Samuel 3:7
7283.text: (As regards Samuel, he had not yet come to know Jehovah, and the word of Jehovah had not yet begun to be revealed to him.)

7284.label: 1 Samuel 3:8
7284.text: So Jehovah called again for the third time: “Samuel!” At that he got up and went to Eʹli and said: “Here I am, for you must have called me.” And Eʹli began to discern that it was Jehovah that was calling the boy.

7285.label: 1 Samuel 3:9
7285.text: Consequently Eʹli said to Samuel: “Go, lie down, and it must occur that, if he should call you, you must say, ‘Speak, Jehovah, for your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

7286.label: 1 Samuel 3:10
7286.text: Then Jehovah came and took his position and called as at the other times: “Samuel, Samuel!” At this Samuel said: “Speak, for your servant is listening.”

7287.label: 1 Samuel 3:11
7287.text: And Jehovah went on to say to Samuel: “Look! I am doing something in Israel which if anyone hears about, both his ears will tingle.

7288.label: 1 Samuel 3:12
7288.text: On that day I shall carry out toward Eʹli all that I have said respecting his house, from beginning to end.

7289.label: 1 Samuel 3:13
7289.text: And you must tell him that I am judging his house to time indefinite for the error that he has known, because his sons are calling down evil upon God, and he has not rebuked them.

7290.label: 1 Samuel 3:14
7290.text: And that is why I have sworn to the house of Eʹli that the error of the house of Eʹli will not be brought to exemption from punishment by sacrifice or by offering to time indefinite.”

7291.label: 1 Samuel 3:15
7291.text: And Samuel continued lying down until the morning. Then he opened the doors of Jehovah’s house. And Samuel was afraid to tell Eʹli of the appearing.

7292.label: 1 Samuel 3:16
7292.text: But Eʹli called Samuel and said: “Samuel, my son!” At this he said: “Here I am.”

7293.label: 1 Samuel 3:17
7293.text: And he went on to say: “What is the word that he has spoken to you? Do not, please, hide it from me. May God do so to you and so may he add to it if you should hide from me a word of all the word that he has spoken to you.”

7294.label: 1 Samuel 3:18
7294.text: So Samuel told him all the words, and he did not hide anything from him. At that he said: “It is Jehovah. What is good in his eyes let him do.”

7295.label: 1 Samuel 3:19
7295.text: And Samuel continued growing up, and Jehovah himself proved to be with him and did not cause any of all his words to fall to the earth.

7296.label: 1 Samuel 3:20
7296.text: And all Israel from Dan to Beʹer-sheʹba became aware that Samuel was one accredited for the position of prophet to Jehovah.

7297.label: 1 Samuel 3:21
7297.text: And Jehovah proceeded to appear again in Shiʹloh, because Jehovah revealed himself to Samuel in Shiʹloh by the word of Jehovah.

7298.label: 1 Samuel 4:1
7298.text: And the word of Samuel continued to come to all Israel. Then Israel went out to meet the Phi·lisʹtines in battle; and they took up camping alongside Eb·en·eʹzer, and the Phi·lisʹtines themselves encamped in Aʹphek.

7299.label: 1 Samuel 4:2
7299.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to draw up in formation to meet Israel, and the battle went badly, so that Israel was defeated before the Phi·lisʹtines, who went striking down about four thousand men in closed battle line in the field.

7300.label: 1 Samuel 4:3
7300.text: When the people came to the camp the older men of Israel began to say: “Why did Jehovah defeat us today before the Phi·lisʹtines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiʹloh the ark of Jehovah’s covenant, that it may come into our midst and may save us from the palm of our enemies.”

7301.label: 1 Samuel 4:4
7301.text: So the people sent to Shiʹloh and carried from there the ark of the covenant of Jehovah of armies, who is sitting upon the cherubs. And the two sons of Eʹli were there with the ark of the covenant of the [true] God, namely, Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has.

7302.label: 1 Samuel 4:5
7302.text: And it came about that as soon as the ark of the covenant of Jehovah came into the camp, all the Israelites broke out into loud shouting, so that the earth was in a stir.

7303.label: 1 Samuel 4:6
7303.text: The Phi·lisʹtines also got to hear the sound of the shouting and began saying: “What does the sound of this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” Finally they got to know that the ark of Jehovah itself had come into the camp.

7304.label: 1 Samuel 4:7
7304.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines became afraid, because, they said: “God has come into the camp!” So they said: “Woe to us, for such a thing as this never occurred before!

7305.label: 1 Samuel 4:8
7305.text: Woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of this majestic God? This is the God that was the smiter of Egypt with every sort of slaughter in the wilderness.

7306.label: 1 Samuel 4:9
7306.text: Show yourselves courageous and prove yourselves men, YOU Phi·lisʹtines, that YOU may not serve the Hebrews just as they have served YOU; and YOU must prove yourselves men and fight!”

7307.label: 1 Samuel 4:10
7307.text: Accordingly the Phi·lisʹtines fought and Israel was defeated, and they went fleeing each one to his tent; and the slaughter came to be very great, so that out of Israel there fell thirty thousand men on foot.

7308.label: 1 Samuel 4:11
7308.text: And the ark of God itself was captured, and the two sons of Eʹli, Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has, died.

7309.label: 1 Samuel 4:12
7309.text: And a man of Benjamin went running from the battle line so that he arrived at Shiʹloh on that day with his garments ripped apart and dirt on his head.

7310.label: 1 Samuel 4:13
7310.text: When he arrived, there was Eʹli sitting on the seat by the roadside, watching, because his heart had become atremble over the ark of the [true] God. And the man himself went in to report in the city, and the whole city began crying out.

7311.label: 1 Samuel 4:14
7311.text: And Eʹli got to hear the sound of the outcry. So he said: “What does the sound of this turmoil mean?” And the man himself hurried that he might go in and report to Eʹli.

7312.label: 1 Samuel 4:15
7312.text: (Now Eʹli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had set so that he was unable to see.)

7313.label: 1 Samuel 4:16
7313.text: And the man proceeded to say to Eʹli: “I am the one coming from the battle line, and I—it is from the battle line that I have fled today.” At this he said: “What is the thing that has happened, my son?”

7314.label: 1 Samuel 4:17
7314.text: So the news bearer answered and said: “Israel has fled before the Phi·lisʹtines, and there has also occurred a great defeat among the people; and also your own two sons have died—Hophʹni and Phinʹe·has —and the very ark of the [true] God has been captured.”

7315.label: 1 Samuel 4:18
7315.text: And it came about that at the moment that he mentioned the ark of the [true] God, he began to fall from the seat backward beside the gate, and his neck got broken so that he died, because the man was old and heavy; and he himself had judged Israel forty years.

7316.label: 1 Samuel 4:19
7316.text: And his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinʹe·has, was pregnant near to giving birth, and she got to hear the report that the ark of the [true] God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband had died. At that she bowed herself and began giving birth, because her pangs came unexpectedly upon her.

7317.label: 1 Samuel 4:20
7317.text: And about the time of her death, the women standing by her began to speak: “Do not be afraid, because it is a son that you have borne.” And she did not answer and did not set her heart on it.

7318.label: 1 Samuel 4:21
7318.text: But she called the boy Ichʹa·bod, saying: “Glory has gone away from Israel into exile,” [this] with reference to the ark of the [true] God’s being captured and with reference to her father-in-law and her husband.

7319.label: 1 Samuel 4:22
7319.text: So she said: “Glory has gone away from Israel into exile, because the ark of the [true] God has been captured.”

7320.label: 1 Samuel 5:1
7320.text: As for the Phi·lisʹtines, they took the ark of the [true] God and then brought it from Eb·en·eʹzer to Ashʹdod.

7321.label: 1 Samuel 5:2
7321.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to take the ark of the [true] God and bring it into the house of Daʹgon and station it beside Daʹgon.

7322.label: 1 Samuel 5:3
7322.text: Then the Ashʹdod·ites got up early the very next day, and there Daʹgon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of Jehovah. So they took Daʹgon and returned him to his place.

7323.label: 1 Samuel 5:4
7323.text: When they got up early in the morning the very day after, there Daʹgon was fallen upon his face to the earth before the ark of Jehovah, with the head of Daʹgon and the palms of both his hands cut off, to the threshold. Only the fish part had been left upon him.

7324.label: 1 Samuel 5:5
7324.text: That is why the priests of Daʹgon and all those going into the house of Daʹgon do not tread upon the threshold of Daʹgon in Ashʹdod down to this day.

7325.label: 1 Samuel 5:6
7325.text: And the hand of Jehovah came to be heavy upon the Ashʹdod·ites, and he began causing panic and striking them with piles, namely, Ashʹdod and its territories.

7326.label: 1 Samuel 5:7
7326.text: And the men of Ashʹdod came to see that it was so, and they said: “Do not let the ark of the God of Israel dwell with us, because his hand has been hard against us and against Daʹgon our god.”

7327.label: 1 Samuel 5:8
7327.text: Consequently they sent and gathered all the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines to them and said: “What shall we do to the ark of the God of Israel?” Finally they said: “Toward Gath let the ark of the God of Israel go around.” So they brought the ark of the God of Israel around to there.

7328.label: 1 Samuel 5:9
7328.text: And it came about that after they had brought it around to there, the hand of Jehovah came to be upon the city with a very great confusion, and he began striking the men of the city, from small to great, and piles began breaking out on them.

7329.label: 1 Samuel 5:10
7329.text: Hence they sent the ark of the [true] God to Ekʹron. And it came about that as soon as the ark of the [true] God came to Ekʹron, the Ekʹron·ites began to cry out, saying: “They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to me to put me and my people to death!”

7330.label: 1 Samuel 5:11
7330.text: Consequently they sent and gathered all the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines and said: “SEND the ark of the God of Israel away that it may return to its place and may not put me and my people to death.” For a death-dealing confusion had occurred in the whole city; the hand of the [true] God had been very heavy there,

7331.label: 1 Samuel 5:12
7331.text: and the men that did not die had been struck with piles. And the cry of the city for help kept ascending to the heavens.

7332.label: 1 Samuel 6:1
7332.text: And the ark of Jehovah proved to be in the field of the Phi·lisʹtines seven months.

7333.label: 1 Samuel 6:2
7333.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to call the priests and the diviners, saying: “What shall we do with the ark of Jehovah? Let us know with what we should send it away to its place.”

7334.label: 1 Samuel 6:3
7334.text: To this they said: “If YOU are sending the ark of the God of Israel away, do not send it away without an offering, for YOU should by all means return to him a guilt offering. Then it is that YOU will be healed, and it must become known to YOU why his hand would not turn away from YOU.”

7335.label: 1 Samuel 6:4
7335.text: At this they said: “What is the guilt offering that we ought to return to him?” Then they said: “According to the number of the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines, five golden piles and five golden jerboas, for every one of YOU and YOUR axis lords have the same scourge.

7336.label: 1 Samuel 6:5
7336.text: And YOU must make images of YOUR piles and images of YOUR jerboas that are bringing the land to ruin, and YOU must give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand from off YOU and YOUR god and YOUR land.

7337.label: 1 Samuel 6:6
7337.text: Also, why should YOU make YOUR heart unresponsive just the way Egypt and Pharʹaoh made their heart unresponsive? Was it not as soon as He dealt severely with them that they proceeded to send them away, and they went their way?

7338.label: 1 Samuel 6:7
7338.text: And now take and make a new wagon, and two cows that are giving suck, upon which no yoke has come up, and YOU must hitch the cows to the wagon, and YOU must make their young ones go back home from following them.

7339.label: 1 Samuel 6:8
7339.text: And YOU must take the ark of Jehovah and place it on the wagon, and the golden articles that YOU must return to him as a guilt offering YOU should put into a box at the side of it. And YOU must send it away, and it must go.

7340.label: 1 Samuel 6:9
7340.text: And YOU must look: if it is the road to its territory that it goes up, to Beth-sheʹmesh, it is he that has done to us this great evil; but if not, we must know that it was not his hand that touched us; an accident it was that happened to us.”

7341.label: 1 Samuel 6:10
7341.text: And the men proceeded to do accordingly. So they took two cows that were giving suck and hitched them to the wagon, and their young ones they shut up at home.

7342.label: 1 Samuel 6:11
7342.text: Then they put the ark of Jehovah upon the wagon, and also the box and the golden jerboas and the images of their piles.

7343.label: 1 Samuel 6:12
7343.text: And the cows began to go straight ahead on the road to Beth-sheʹmesh. On the one highway they went, lowing as they went, and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left. All the while the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines were walking after them as far as the boundary of Beth-sheʹmesh.

7344.label: 1 Samuel 6:13
7344.text: And people of Beth-sheʹmesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the low plain. When they raised their eyes and saw the Ark, they gave way to rejoicing at seeing it.

7345.label: 1 Samuel 6:14
7345.text: And the wagon itself came into the field of Joshua the Beth-sheʹmite and kept standing there, where there was a large stone. And they went splitting up the wood of the wagon, and the cows they offered up as a burnt offering to Jehovah.

7346.label: 1 Samuel 6:15
7346.text: And the Levites themselves took the ark of Jehovah down and the box that was with it, in which the golden articles were, and they proceeded to put it upon the large stone. And the men of Beth-sheʹmesh, for their part, offered up burnt offerings, and they continued rendering up sacrifices on that day to Jehovah.

7347.label: 1 Samuel 6:16
7347.text: And the five axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines themselves saw it and went their way back to Ekʹron on that day.

7348.label: 1 Samuel 6:17
7348.text: Now these are the golden piles that the Phi·lisʹtines returned as a guilt offering to Jehovah: for Ashʹdod one, for Gaʹza one, for Ashʹke·lon one, for Gath one, for Ekʹron one.

7349.label: 1 Samuel 6:18
7349.text: And the golden jerboas were to the number of all the cities of the Phi·lisʹtines belonging to the five axis lords, from the fortified city to the village of the open country. And the great stone upon which they rested the ark of Jehovah is a witness down to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-sheʹmite.

7350.label: 1 Samuel 6:19
7350.text: And he went striking down the men of Beth-sheʹmesh, because they had looked upon the ark of Jehovah. So he struck down among the people seventy men—fifty thousand men —and the people began mourning because Jehovah had struck down the people with a great slaughter.

7351.label: 1 Samuel 6:20
7351.text: Further, the men of Beth-sheʹmesh said: “Who will be able to stand before Jehovah this holy God, and to whom will he withdraw from off us?”

7352.label: 1 Samuel 6:21
7352.text: Finally they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim, saying: “The Phi·lisʹtines have returned the ark of Jehovah. Come down. Take it up to yourselves.”

7353.label: 1 Samuel 7:1
7353.text: Accordingly the men of Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim came and brought the ark of Jehovah up and took it into the house of A·binʹa·dab on the hill, and El·e·aʹzar his son was the one whom they sanctified to guard the ark of Jehovah.

7354.label: 1 Samuel 7:2
7354.text: And it came about that from the day of the Ark’s dwelling in Kirʹi·ath-jeʹa·rim the days kept multiplying, so that they amounted to twenty years, and all the house of Israel went lamenting after Jehovah.

7355.label: 1 Samuel 7:3
7355.text: And Samuel proceeded to say to all the house of Israel: “If it is with all YOUR heart YOU are returning to Jehovah, put away the foreign gods from YOUR midst and also the Ashʹto·reth images, and direct YOUR heart unswervingly to Jehovah and serve him alone, and he will deliver YOU from the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.”

7356.label: 1 Samuel 7:4
7356.text: At that the sons of Israel put away the Baʹals and the Ashʹto·reth images and began serving Jehovah alone.

7357.label: 1 Samuel 7:5
7357.text: Then Samuel said: “Collect all Israel together at Mizʹpah, that I may pray in YOUR behalf to Jehovah.”

7358.label: 1 Samuel 7:6
7358.text: So they were collected together at Mizʹpah, and they went drawing water and pouring it out before Jehovah and kept a fast on that day. And they began saying there: “We have sinned against Jehovah.” And Samuel took up judging the sons of Israel in Mizʹpah.

7359.label: 1 Samuel 7:7
7359.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines came to hear that the sons of Israel had collected themselves together at Mizʹpah, and the axis lords of the Phi·lisʹtines got on their way up against Israel. When the sons of Israel heard of it, they began to be afraid on account of the Phi·lisʹtines.

7360.label: 1 Samuel 7:8
7360.text: So the sons of Israel said to Samuel: “Do not keep silent for our sakes from calling to Jehovah our God for aid, that he may save us from the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.”

7361.label: 1 Samuel 7:9
7361.text: Then Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it up as a burnt offering, a whole offering, to Jehovah; and Samuel began calling to Jehovah for aid in behalf of Israel, and Jehovah proceeded to answer him.

7362.label: 1 Samuel 7:10
7362.text: And it came about that while Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Phi·lisʹtines themselves drew near for battle against Israel. And Jehovah now caused it to thunder with a loud noise on that day against the Phi·lisʹtines, that he might throw them into confusion; and they got defeated before Israel.

7363.label: 1 Samuel 7:11
7363.text: At that the men of Israel sallied forth from Mizʹpah and went in pursuit of the Phi·lisʹtines and kept striking them down as far as south of Beth-car.

7364.label: 1 Samuel 7:12
7364.text: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizʹpah and Jeshʹa·nah and began to call its name Eb·en·eʹzer. Accordingly he said: “Till now Jehovah has helped us.”

7365.label: 1 Samuel 7:13
7365.text: Thus the Phi·lisʹtines were subdued, and they did not come anymore into the territory of Israel; and the hand of Jehovah continued to be against the Phi·lisʹtines all the days of Samuel.

7366.label: 1 Samuel 7:14
7366.text: And the cities that the Phi·lisʹtines had taken from Israel kept coming back to Israel from Ekʹron to Gath, and the territory of them Israel delivered from the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines. And there came to be peace between Israel and the Amʹor·ites.

7367.label: 1 Samuel 7:15
7367.text: And Samuel kept on judging Israel all the days of his life.

7368.label: 1 Samuel 7:16
7368.text: And he traveled from year to year and made the circuit of Bethʹel and Gilʹgal and Mizʹpah and judged Israel at all these places.

7369.label: 1 Samuel 7:17
7369.text: But his return was to Raʹmah, because there was where his house was, and there he judged Israel. And he proceeded to build an altar there to Jehovah.

7370.label: 1 Samuel 8:1
7370.text: And it came about that as soon as Samuel had grown old he made appointments of his sons as judges for Israel.

7371.label: 1 Samuel 8:2
7371.text: Now the name of his firstborn son happened to be Joel, and the name of his second A·biʹjah; they were judging in Beʹer-sheʹba.

7372.label: 1 Samuel 8:3
7372.text: And his sons did not walk in his ways, but they were inclined to follow unjust profit and would accept a bribe and pervert judgment.

7373.label: 1 Samuel 8:4
7373.text: In time all the older men of Israel collected themselves together and came to Samuel at Raʹmah

7374.label: 1 Samuel 8:5
7374.text: and said to him: “Look! You yourself have grown old, but your own sons have not walked in your ways. Now do appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

7375.label: 1 Samuel 8:6
7375.text: But the thing was bad in the eyes of Samuel inasmuch as they had said: “Do give us a king to judge us,” and Samuel began to pray to Jehovah.

7376.label: 1 Samuel 8:7
7376.text: Then Jehovah said to Samuel: “Listen to the voice of the people as respects all that they say to you; for it is not you whom they have rejected, but it is I whom they have rejected from being king over them.

7377.label: 1 Samuel 8:8
7377.text: In accord with all their doings that they have done from the day of my bringing them up out of Egypt until this day in that they kept leaving me and serving other gods, that is the way they are doing also to you.

7378.label: 1 Samuel 8:9
7378.text: And now listen to their voice. Only this, that you should solemnly warn them, and you must tell them the rightful due of the king who will reign over them.”

7379.label: 1 Samuel 8:10
7379.text: So Samuel said all the words of Jehovah to the people who were asking a king of him.

7380.label: 1 Samuel 8:11
7380.text: And he proceeded to say: “This will become the rightful due of the king that will reign over YOU: YOUR sons he will take and put them as his in his chariots and among his horsemen, and some will have to run before his chariots;

7381.label: 1 Samuel 8:12
7381.text: and to appoint for himself chiefs over thousands and chiefs over fifties, and [some] to do his plowing and to reap his harvest and to make his war instruments and his chariot instruments.

7382.label: 1 Samuel 8:13
7382.text: And YOUR daughters he will take for ointment mixers and cooks and bakers.

7383.label: 1 Samuel 8:14
7383.text: And YOUR fields and YOUR vineyards and YOUR olive groves, the best ones, he will take and actually give to his servants.

7384.label: 1 Samuel 8:15
7384.text: And of YOUR fields of seed and of YOUR vineyards he will take the tenth, and he will certainly give [them] to his court officials and his servants.

7385.label: 1 Samuel 8:16
7385.text: And YOUR menservants and YOUR maidservants and YOUR best herds, and YOUR asses he will take, and he will have to use them for his work.

7386.label: 1 Samuel 8:17
7386.text: Of YOUR flocks he will take the tenth, and YOU yourselves will become his as servants.

7387.label: 1 Samuel 8:18
7387.text: And YOU will certainly cry out in that day by reason of YOUR king, whom YOU have chosen for yourselves, but Jehovah will not answer YOU in that day.”

7388.label: 1 Samuel 8:19
7388.text: However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel and said: “No, but a king is what will come to be over us.

7389.label: 1 Samuel 8:20
7389.text: And we must become, we also, like all the nations, and our king must judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.”

7390.label: 1 Samuel 8:21
7390.text: And Samuel gave a hearing to all the words of the people; then he spoke them in the ears of Jehovah.

7391.label: 1 Samuel 8:22
7391.text: And Jehovah proceeded to say to Samuel: “Listen to their voice, and you must cause a king to reign for them.” Accordingly Samuel said to the men of Israel: “Go each one to his city.”

7392.label: 1 Samuel 9:1
7392.text: Now there happened to be a man of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, the son of A·biʹel, the son of Zeʹror, the son of Be·coʹrath, the son of A·phiʹah, a Benʹja·min·ite, a man mighty in wealth.

7393.label: 1 Samuel 9:2
7393.text: And he happened to have a son whose name was Saul, young and handsome, and there was no man of the sons of Israel that was handsomer than he; from his shoulders upward he was taller than all the people.

7394.label: 1 Samuel 9:3
7394.text: And the she-asses belonging to Kish the father of Saul got lost. So Kish said to Saul his son: “Take, please, with you one of the attendants and get up, go, look for the she-asses.”

7395.label: 1 Samuel 9:4
7395.text: And he went passing through the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im and passing on through the land of Shalʹi·shah, and they did not find [them]. And they went passing on through the land of Shaʹa·lim, but they were not [there]. And he went passing on through the land of the Benʹja·min·ites, and they did not find [them].

7396.label: 1 Samuel 9:5
7396.text: They themselves came into the land of Zuph; and Saul, for his part, said to his attendant that was with him: “Do come, and let us return, that my father may not quit attending to the she-asses and actually become anxious about us.”

7397.label: 1 Samuel 9:6
7397.text: But he said to him: “Look, please! There is a man of God in this city, and the man is held in honor. All that he says comes true without fail. Let us go there now. Perhaps he can tell us our way that we must go.”

7398.label: 1 Samuel 9:7
7398.text: At this Saul said to his attendant: “And if we should go, what shall we bring to the man? because the bread itself has disappeared from our receptacles, and, as a gift, there is nothing to bring to the man of the [true] God. What is there with us?”

7399.label: 1 Samuel 9:8
7399.text: So the attendant answered Saul once more and said: “Look! There is a quarter of a shekel of silver found in my hand, and I shall have to give it to the man of the [true] God, and he will have to tell us our way.”

7400.label: 1 Samuel 9:9
7400.text: (In former times in Israel this was the way the man would have talked on his going to seek God: “COME, and let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today used to be called a seer in former times.)

7401.label: 1 Samuel 9:10
7401.text: Then Saul said to his attendant: “Your word is good. Do come, let us go.” And they went their way to the city where the man of the [true] God was.

7402.label: 1 Samuel 9:11
7402.text: While they were going up on the ascent to the city, they themselves found girls going out to draw water. So they said to them: “Is the seer in this place?”

7403.label: 1 Samuel 9:12
7403.text: Then they answered them and said: “He is. Look! He is ahead of you. Hurry now, because today he has come to the city, for there is a sacrifice today for the people on the high place.

7404.label: 1 Samuel 9:13
7404.text: As soon as YOU men come into the city, YOU will directly find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; because the people may not eat until his coming, for he is the one that blesses the sacrifice. First after that those who are invited may eat. And now GO up, because him—just now YOU will find him.”

7405.label: 1 Samuel 9:14
7405.text: Accordingly they went on up to the city. As they were coming into the middle of the city, why, there was Samuel coming out to meet them to go up to the high place.

7406.label: 1 Samuel 9:15
7406.text: As for Jehovah, he had uncovered the ear of Samuel the day before Saul came, saying:

7407.label: 1 Samuel 9:16
7407.text: “Tomorrow about this time I shall send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you must anoint him as leader over my people Israel; and he must save my people from the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines, because I have seen [the affliction of] my people, for their outcry has come to me.”

7408.label: 1 Samuel 9:17
7408.text: And Samuel himself saw Saul, and Jehovah, for his part, answered him: “Here is the man of whom I said to you, ‘This is the one that will keep my people within bounds.’”

7409.label: 1 Samuel 9:18
7409.text: Then Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said: “Do tell me, please, Just where is the house of the seer?”

7410.label: 1 Samuel 9:19
7410.text: And Samuel proceeded to answer Saul and say: “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, and YOU men must eat with me today, and I must send you away in the morning, and all that is in your heart I shall tell you.

7411.label: 1 Samuel 9:20
7411.text: As regards the she-asses that were lost to you three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And to whom does all that is desirable of Israel belong? Is it not to you and to the whole house of your father?”

7412.label: 1 Samuel 9:21
7412.text: At this Saul answered and said: “Am I not a Benʹja·min·ite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the most insignificant of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? So why have you spoken to me a thing like this?”

7413.label: 1 Samuel 9:22
7413.text: Then Samuel took Saul and his attendant and brought them to the dining hall and gave them a place at the head of those invited; and they were about thirty men.

7414.label: 1 Samuel 9:23
7414.text: Later Samuel said to the cook: “Do give the portion that I have given to you, of which I said to you, ‘Put it away by you.’”

7415.label: 1 Samuel 9:24
7415.text: At that the cook lifted off the leg and what was on it, and put it before Saul. And he went on to say: “Here is what has been reserved. Put it before yourself. Eat, because to the appointed time they have reserved it for you that you may eat with those invited.” So Saul ate with Samuel on that day.

7416.label: 1 Samuel 9:25
7416.text: Subsequently they went down from the high place to the city, and he continued speaking with Saul on the housetop.

7417.label: 1 Samuel 9:26
7417.text: Then they rose early, and it came about that as soon as the dawn ascended Samuel proceeded to call to Saul on the housetop, saying: “Do get up, that I may send you away.” So Saul got up and both of them, he and Samuel, went forth out of doors.

7418.label: 1 Samuel 9:27
7418.text: While they were descending by the edge of the city Samuel himself said to Saul: “Say to the attendant that he should pass on ahead of us”—so he passed on—“and, as for you, stand still now that I may let you hear the word of God.”

7419.label: 1 Samuel 10:1
7419.text: Samuel then took the flask of oil and poured it out upon his head and kissed him and said: “Is it not because Jehovah has anointed you as a leader over his inheritance?

7420.label: 1 Samuel 10:2
7420.text: On your going away from me today you will certainly find two men close by the tomb of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin at Zelʹzah, and they will certainly say to you, ‘The she-asses that you have gone to look for have been found, but now your father has given up the matter of the she-asses and has become anxious about YOU men, saying: “What shall I do about my son?”’

7421.label: 1 Samuel 10:3
7421.text: And you must pass on from there still farther and come as far as the big tree of Taʹbor, and there there must encounter you three men going up to the [true] God at Bethʹel, one carrying three kids and one carrying three round loaves of bread and one carrying a large jar of wine.

7422.label: 1 Samuel 10:4
7422.text: And they will certainly ask about your welfare and give you two loaves, and you must accept them from their hand.

7423.label: 1 Samuel 10:5
7423.text: It is after that that you will come to the hill of the [true] God, where there is a garrison of the Phi·lisʹtines. And it should come about that at the time of your coming there to the city, you will certainly meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, and ahead of them a stringed instrument and tambourine and flute and harp, while they are speaking as prophets.

7424.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
7424.text: And the spirit of Jehovah will certainly become operative upon you, and you will certainly speak as a prophet along with them and be changed into another man.

7425.label: 1 Samuel 10:7
7425.text: And it must occur that when these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds possible, because the [true] God is with you.

7426.label: 1 Samuel 10:8
7426.text: And you must go down ahead of me to Gilʹgal; and, look! I am going down to you to offer up burnt sacrifices, to render up communion sacrifices. Seven days you should keep waiting until my coming to you, and I shall certainly let you know what you should do.”

7427.label: 1 Samuel 10:9
7427.text: And it occurred that as soon as he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, God began changing the heart of his into another; and all these signs proceeded to come true on that day.

7428.label: 1 Samuel 10:10
7428.text: So they went from there to the hill, and here there was a group of prophets to meet him; at once the spirit of God became operative upon him, and he began to speak as a prophet in the middle of them.

7429.label: 1 Samuel 10:11
7429.text: And it came about that when all those knowing him formerly saw him, look! it was with prophets that he prophesied. Consequently the people said one to another: “What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

7430.label: 1 Samuel 10:12
7430.text: Then a man from there answered and said: “But who is their father?” That is why it has become a proverbial saying: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

7431.label: 1 Samuel 10:13
7431.text: At length he finished speaking as a prophet and came to the high place.

7432.label: 1 Samuel 10:14
7432.text: Later the brother of Saul’s father said to him and to his attendant: “Where did YOU go?” Upon that he said: “To look for the she-asses, and we kept on going to see, but they were not [there]. So we came to Samuel.”

7433.label: 1 Samuel 10:15
7433.text: At this Saul’s uncle said: “Do tell me, please, What did Samuel say to YOU men?”

7434.label: 1 Samuel 10:16
7434.text: In turn Saul said to his uncle: “He told us unmistakably that the she-asses had been found.” And the matter of the kingship about which Samuel had talked, he did not tell him.

7435.label: 1 Samuel 10:17
7435.text: And Samuel proceeded to call the people together to Jehovah at Mizʹpah

7436.label: 1 Samuel 10:18
7436.text: and to say to the sons of Israel: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘It was I who brought Israel up out of Egypt and who went delivering YOU from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing YOU.

7437.label: 1 Samuel 10:19
7437.text: But YOU—today YOU have rejected YOUR God who was a savior to YOU out of all YOUR evils and YOUR distresses, and YOU went on to say: “No, but a king is what you should put over us.” And now take YOUR stand before Jehovah by YOUR tribes and by YOUR thousands.’”

7438.label: 1 Samuel 10:20
7438.text: Accordingly Samuel had all the tribes of Israel draw near, and the tribe of Benjamin came to be picked.

7439.label: 1 Samuel 10:21
7439.text: Then he had the tribe of Benjamin draw near by its families, and the family of the Matʹrites came to be picked. Finally Saul the son of Kish came to be picked. And they went looking for him, and he was not to be found.

7440.label: 1 Samuel 10:22
7440.text: Hence they inquired further of Jehovah: “Has the man come here as yet?” To this Jehovah said: “Here he is, hidden among the luggage.”

7441.label: 1 Samuel 10:23
7441.text: So they went running and took him from there. When he took his stand in the middle of the people, he was taller than all the other people from his shoulders upward.

7442.label: 1 Samuel 10:24
7442.text: Then Samuel said to all the people: “Have YOU seen the one whom Jehovah has chosen, that there is none like him among all the people?” And all the people began to shout and say: “Let the king live!”

7443.label: 1 Samuel 10:25
7443.text: Upon that Samuel spoke to the people about the rightful due of the kingship and wrote it in a book and deposited it before Jehovah. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each one to his house.

7444.label: 1 Samuel 10:26
7444.text: As for Saul himself, he went to his home at Gibʹe·ah, and the valiant men whose heart God had touched proceeded to go with him.

7445.label: 1 Samuel 10:27
7445.text: As for the good-for-nothing men, they said: “How will this one save us?” Accordingly they despised him, and they did not bring any gift to him. But he continued like one grown speechless.

7446.label: 1 Samuel 11:1
7446.text: And Naʹhash the Amʹmon·ite proceeded to go up and camp against Jaʹbesh in Gilʹe·ad. At that all the men of Jaʹbesh said to Naʹhash: “Conclude a covenant with us that we may serve you.”

7447.label: 1 Samuel 11:2
7447.text: Then Naʹhash the Amʹmon·ite said to them: “On this condition I shall conclude it with YOU, on the condition of boring out every right eye of YOURS, and I must put it as a reproach upon all Israel.”

7448.label: 1 Samuel 11:3
7448.text: In turn the older men of Jaʹbesh said to him: “Give us seven days’ time, and we will send messengers into all the territory of Israel and, if there is no savior of us, we must then go out to you.”

7449.label: 1 Samuel 11:4
7449.text: In time the messengers came to Gibʹe·ah of Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people, and all the people began raising their voice and weeping.

7450.label: 1 Samuel 11:5
7450.text: But here is Saul coming after the herd from the field, and Saul proceeded to say: “What is the matter with the people, that they should weep?” And they began relating to him the words of the men of Jaʹbesh.

7451.label: 1 Samuel 11:6
7451.text: And the spirit of God became operative upon Saul on his hearing these words, and his anger got very hot.

7452.label: 1 Samuel 11:7
7452.text: So he took a pair of bulls and cut them in pieces and sent these into all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying: “Whoever of us is not going out as a follower of Saul and of Samuel, this is the way it will be done to his cattle!” And the dread of Jehovah began to fall upon the people so that they came out as one man.

7453.label: 1 Samuel 11:8
7453.text: Then he took the sum of them in Beʹzek, and the sons of Israel amounted to three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

7454.label: 1 Samuel 11:9
7454.text: They now said to the messengers that had come: “This is what YOU will say to the men of Jaʹbesh in Gilʹe·ad, ‘Tomorrow salvation will take place for YOU when the sun gets hot.’” With that the messengers came and told the men of Jaʹbesh, and they gave way to rejoicing.

7455.label: 1 Samuel 11:10
7455.text: Accordingly the men of Jaʹbesh said: “Tomorrow we shall come out to YOU people, and YOU must do to us in harmony with all that is good in YOUR eyes.”

7456.label: 1 Samuel 11:11
7456.text: And it came about on the next day that Saul proceeded to put the people into three bands; and they made their way into the middle of the camp during the morning watch and went striking down the Amʹmon·ites till the day grew hot. When there proved to be some that were left over, then they were sent scattering and there were not left over among them two together.

7457.label: 1 Samuel 11:12
7457.text: And the people began to say to Samuel: “Who is it saying, ‘Saul—is he to be king over us?’ GIVE the men over, that we may put them to death.”

7458.label: 1 Samuel 11:13
7458.text: However, Saul said: “Not a man should be put to death on this day, because today Jehovah has performed salvation in Israel.”

7459.label: 1 Samuel 11:14
7459.text: Later Samuel said to the people: “Come and let us go to Gilʹgal that we may there make the kingship anew.”

7460.label: 1 Samuel 11:15
7460.text: So all the people went to Gilʹgal, and there they proceeded to make Saul king before Jehovah in Gilʹgal. Then they rendered up communion sacrifices there before Jehovah, and there Saul and all the men of Israel continued rejoicing to a great degree.

7461.label: 1 Samuel 12:1
7461.text: Finally Samuel said to all Israel: “Here I have listened to YOUR voice as respects all that YOU have said to me, that I should cause a king to reign over YOU.

7462.label: 1 Samuel 12:2
7462.text: And now here is the king walking before YOU! As for me, I have grown old and gray, and my sons, here they are with YOU, and I—I have walked before YOU from my youth until this day.

7463.label: 1 Samuel 12:3
7463.text: Here I am. Answer against me in front of Jehovah and in front of his anointed one: Whose bull have I taken or whose ass have I taken or whom have I defrauded or whom have I crushed or from whose hand have I accepted hush money that I should hide my eyes with it? And I shall make restoration to YOU people.”

7464.label: 1 Samuel 12:4
7464.text: To this they said: “You have not defrauded us, nor have you crushed us, nor have you accepted anything at all from the hand of a single one.”

7465.label: 1 Samuel 12:5
7465.text: So he said to them: “Jehovah is a witness against YOU, and his anointed one is a witness this day that YOU have found nothing at all in my hand.” To this they said: “He is a witness.”

7466.label: 1 Samuel 12:6
7466.text: And Samuel went on to say to the people: “Jehovah [is a witness], who used Moses and Aaron and who brought YOUR forefathers up out of the land of Egypt.

7467.label: 1 Samuel 12:7
7467.text: And now take YOUR stand, and I will judge YOU before Jehovah [and recount to YOU] all the righteous acts of Jehovah that he has done with YOU and with YOUR forefathers.

7468.label: 1 Samuel 12:8
7468.text: “As soon as Jacob had come into Egypt and YOUR forefathers began calling to Jehovah for aid, Jehovah proceeded to send Moses and Aaron, that they might lead YOUR forefathers out from Egypt and cause them to dwell in this place.

7469.label: 1 Samuel 12:9
7469.text: And they went forgetting Jehovah their God, so that he sold them into the hand of Sisʹe·ra the chief of the army of Haʹzor and into the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines and into the hand of the king of Moʹab, and they kept fighting against them.

7470.label: 1 Samuel 12:10
7470.text: And they began to call to Jehovah for aid and say, ‘We have sinned, for we have left Jehovah that we might serve the Baʹals and the Ashʹto·reth images; and now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, that we may serve you.’

7471.label: 1 Samuel 12:11
7471.text: And Jehovah proceeded to send Jer·ub·baʹal and Beʹdan and Jephʹthah and Samuel and deliver YOU out of the hand of YOUR enemies all around, that YOU might dwell in security.

7472.label: 1 Samuel 12:12
7472.text: When YOU saw that Naʹhash the king of the sons of Amʹmon had come against YOU, YOU kept saying to me, ‘No, but a king is what should reign over us!’ all the while Jehovah YOUR God being YOUR King.

7473.label: 1 Samuel 12:13
7473.text: And now here is the king whom YOU have chosen, for whom YOU asked; and here Jehovah has put over YOU a king.

7474.label: 1 Samuel 12:14
7474.text: If YOU will fear Jehovah and actually serve him and obey his voice, and YOU will not rebel against the order of Jehovah, both YOU and the king who must reign over YOU will certainly prove to be followers of Jehovah YOUR God.

7475.label: 1 Samuel 12:15
7475.text: But if YOU will not obey the voice of Jehovah and YOU will actually rebel against the order of Jehovah, the hand of Jehovah will certainly prove to be against YOU and YOUR fathers.

7476.label: 1 Samuel 12:16
7476.text: Now, also, take YOUR stand and see this great thing that Jehovah is doing before YOUR eyes.

7477.label: 1 Samuel 12:17
7477.text: Is it not wheat harvest today? I shall call to Jehovah that he may give thunders and rain; then know and see that YOUR evil is abundant that YOU have done in the eyes of Jehovah in asking for yourselves a king.”

7478.label: 1 Samuel 12:18
7478.text: Upon that Samuel called to Jehovah, and Jehovah proceeded to give thunders and rain on that day, so that all the people were greatly in fear of Jehovah and of Samuel.

7479.label: 1 Samuel 12:19
7479.text: And all the people began to say to Samuel: “Pray in behalf of your servants to Jehovah your God, as we do not want to die; because we have added to all our sins an evil in asking for ourselves a king.”

7480.label: 1 Samuel 12:20
7480.text: So Samuel said to the people: “Do not be afraid. YOU—YOU have done all this evil. Only do not turn aside from following Jehovah, and YOU must serve Jehovah with all YOUR heart.

7481.label: 1 Samuel 12:21
7481.text: And YOU must not turn aside to follow the unrealities that are of no benefit and that do not deliver, because they are unrealities.

7482.label: 1 Samuel 12:22
7482.text: For Jehovah will not desert his people for the sake of his great name, because Jehovah has taken it upon himself to make YOU his people.

7483.label: 1 Samuel 12:23
7483.text: As for me also, it is unthinkable, on my part, to sin against Jehovah by ceasing to pray in YOUR behalf; and I must instruct YOU in the good and right way.

7484.label: 1 Samuel 12:24
7484.text: Only fear Jehovah, and YOU must serve him in truth with all YOUR heart; for see what great things he has done for YOU.

7485.label: 1 Samuel 12:25
7485.text: But if YOU flagrantly do what is bad, YOU will be swept away, both YOU and YOUR king.”

7486.label: 1 Samuel 13:1
7486.text: Saul was [?] years old when he began to reign, and for two years he reigned over Israel.

7487.label: 1 Samuel 13:2
7487.text: And Saul proceeded to choose for himself three thousand men out of Israel; and two thousand came to be with Saul at Michʹmash and in the mountainous region of Bethʹel, and a thousand proved to be with Jonʹa·than at Gibʹe·ah of Benjamin, and the rest of the people he sent away, each one to his tent.

7488.label: 1 Samuel 13:3
7488.text: Then Jonʹa·than struck down the garrison of the Phi·lisʹtines that was in Geʹba; and the Phi·lisʹtines got to hear of it. As for Saul, he had the horn blown throughout all the land, saying: “Let the Hebrews hear!”

7489.label: 1 Samuel 13:4
7489.text: And all Israel itself heard tell: “Saul has struck down a garrison of the Phi·lisʹtines, and now Israel has become foul-smelling among the Phi·lisʹtines.” So the people were called together to follow Saul to Gilʹgal.

7490.label: 1 Samuel 13:5
7490.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines, for their part, collected themselves together to fight against Israel, thirty thousand war chariots and six thousand horsemen and people like the grains of sand that are upon the seashore for multitude; and they went their way up and began camping in Michʹmash to the east of Beth-aʹven.

7491.label: 1 Samuel 13:6
7491.text: And the men of Israel themselves saw that they were in sore straits, because the people were hard pressed; and the people went hiding themselves in the caves and the hollows and the crags and the vaults and the waterpits.

7492.label: 1 Samuel 13:7
7492.text: Hebrews even crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilʹe·ad. But Saul himself was yet in Gilʹgal, and all the people trembled while following him.

7493.label: 1 Samuel 13:8
7493.text: And he continued waiting for seven days to the appointed time that Samuel [had said]; and Samuel did not come to Gilʹgal, and the people were scattering from him.

7494.label: 1 Samuel 13:9
7494.text: Finally Saul said: “BRING near to me the burnt sacrifice and the communion sacrifices.” With that he went offering up the burnt sacrifice.

7495.label: 1 Samuel 13:10
7495.text: And it came about that as soon as he had finished offering up the burnt sacrifice, why, there was Samuel coming in. So Saul went out to meet him and bless him.

7496.label: 1 Samuel 13:11
7496.text: Then Samuel said: “What is it you have done?” To this Saul said: “I saw that the people had been dispersed from me, and you—you did not come within the appointed days, and the Phi·lisʹtines were being collected together at Michʹmash,

7497.label: 1 Samuel 13:12
7497.text: so I said to myself, ‘Now the Phi·lisʹtines will come down against me at Gilʹgal, and the face of Jehovah I have not softened.’ So I compelled myself and went offering up the burnt sacrifice.”

7498.label: 1 Samuel 13:13
7498.text: At this Samuel said to Saul: “You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of Jehovah your God that he commanded you, because, if you had, Jehovah would have made your kingdom firm over Israel to time indefinite.

7499.label: 1 Samuel 13:14
7499.text: And now your kingdom will not last. Jehovah will certainly find for himself a man agreeable to his heart; and Jehovah will commission him as a leader over his people, because you did not keep what Jehovah commanded you.”

7500.label: 1 Samuel 13:15
7500.text: Then Samuel rose and went his way up from Gilʹgal to Gibʹe·ah of Benjamin, and Saul proceeded to take the count of the people, those yet found with him, about six hundred men.

7501.label: 1 Samuel 13:16
7501.text: And Saul and Jonʹa·than his son and the people yet found with them were dwelling in Geʹba of Benjamin. As for the Phi·lisʹtines, they had encamped in Michʹmash.

7502.label: 1 Samuel 13:17
7502.text: And the force of pillagers would sally forth from the camp of the Phi·lisʹtines in three bands. The one band would turn to the road to Ophʹrah, to the land of Shuʹal,

7503.label: 1 Samuel 13:18
7503.text: and the other band would turn to the road of Beth-hoʹron, and the third band would turn to the road to the boundary that looks toward the valley of Ze·boʹim, toward the wilderness.

7504.label: 1 Samuel 13:19
7504.text: Now there was not a smith to be found in all the land of Israel, because the Phi·lisʹtines had said: “That the Hebrews may not make a sword or a spear.”

7505.label: 1 Samuel 13:20
7505.text: And all the Israelites would go down to the Phi·lisʹtines to get each one his plowshare or his mattock or his ax or his sickle sharpened.

7506.label: 1 Samuel 13:21
7506.text: And the price for sharpening proved to be a pim for the plowshares and for the mattocks and for the three-toothed instruments and for the axes and for fixing fast the oxgoad.

7507.label: 1 Samuel 13:22
7507.text: And it happened on the day of battle that not a sword or a spear was found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonʹa·than; but there could be found one belonging to Saul and to Jonʹa·than his son.

7508.label: 1 Samuel 13:23
7508.text: Now an outpost of the Phi·lisʹtines would sally forth to the ravine pass of Michʹmash.

7509.label: 1 Samuel 14:1
7509.text: And it came about one day that Jonʹa·than the son of Saul proceeded to say to the attendant carrying his weapons: “Do come and let us cross over to the outpost of the Phi·lisʹtines who are across over there.” But to his father he did not tell it.

7510.label: 1 Samuel 14:2
7510.text: And Saul was dwelling at the outskirts of Gibʹe·ah under the pomegranate tree that is in Migʹron; and the people that were with him were about six hundred men.

7511.label: 1 Samuel 14:3
7511.text: (And A·hiʹjah the son of A·hiʹtub, the brother of Ichʹa·bod, the son of Phinʹe·has, the son of Eʹli, the priest of Jehovah in Shiʹloh, was carrying the ephʹod.) And the people themselves did not know that Jonʹa·than had gone.

7512.label: 1 Samuel 14:4
7512.text: Now between the passages that Jonʹa·than looked for to cross over against the outpost of the Phi·lisʹtines there was a toothlike crag here on this side and a toothlike crag there on that side, and the name of the one was Boʹzez and the name of the other was Seʹneh.

7513.label: 1 Samuel 14:5
7513.text: The one tooth was a pillar on the north facing Michʹmash, and the other was on the south facing Geʹba.

7514.label: 1 Samuel 14:6
7514.text: So Jonʹa·than said to the attendant, his armor-bearer: “Do come and let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps Jehovah will work for us, for there is no hindrance to Jehovah to save by many or by few.”

7515.label: 1 Samuel 14:7
7515.text: At this his armor-bearer said to him: “Do whatever is in your heart. Turn where you wish to. Here I am with you in accord with your heart.”

7516.label: 1 Samuel 14:8
7516.text: Then Jonʹa·than said: “Here we are crossing over to the men, and let us expose ourselves to them.

7517.label: 1 Samuel 14:9
7517.text: If this is the way they should say to us, ‘Stand still until we make contact with YOU!’ we must then stand where we are, and we should not go on up to them.

7518.label: 1 Samuel 14:10
7518.text: But if this is the way they should say, ‘Come up against us!’ we must then go up, because Jehovah will certainly give them into our hand, and this is for us the sign.”

7519.label: 1 Samuel 14:11
7519.text: With that the two of them exposed themselves to the outpost of the Phi·lisʹtines. And the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to say: “Here are the Hebrews coming out from the holes where they have hidden themselves.”

7520.label: 1 Samuel 14:12
7520.text: So the men of the outpost answered Jonʹa·than and his armor-bearer and said: “Come on up to us, and we will let YOU know a thing!” At once Jonʹa·than said to his armor-bearer: “Come up after me, because Jehovah will certainly give them into the hand of Israel.”

7521.label: 1 Samuel 14:13
7521.text: And Jonʹa·than kept going up on his hands and his feet, and his armor-bearer after him; and they began to fall before Jonʹa·than, and his armor-bearer was putting them to death behind him.

7522.label: 1 Samuel 14:14
7522.text: And the first slaughter with which Jonʹa·than and his armor-bearer struck them down amounted to about twenty men within about half the plowing line in an acre of field.

7523.label: 1 Samuel 14:15
7523.text: Then a trembling occurred in the camp in the field and among all the people of the outpost; and the force of pillagers trembled, even they, and the earth began quaking, and it developed into a trembling from God.

7524.label: 1 Samuel 14:16
7524.text: And the watchmen belonging to Saul in Gibʹe·ah of Benjamin got to see it, and, look! the turmoil swayed this way and that.

7525.label: 1 Samuel 14:17
7525.text: And Saul proceeded to say to the people that were with him: “Take the count, please, and see who has gone out from us.” When they took the count, why, look! Jonʹa·than and his armor-bearer were not there.

7526.label: 1 Samuel 14:18
7526.text: Saul now said to A·hiʹjah: “Do bring the ark of the [true] God near!” (For the ark of the [true] God proved to be on that day with the sons of Israel.)

7527.label: 1 Samuel 14:19
7527.text: And it came about that while Saul was speaking to the priest, the turmoil that was in the camp of the Phi·lisʹtines continued to go on, getting greater and greater. Then Saul said to the priest: “Withdraw your hand.”

7528.label: 1 Samuel 14:20
7528.text: Thus Saul and all the people that were with him were called out. So they came as far as the battle, and there the sword of each one had come to be against his fellowman; the rout was very great.

7529.label: 1 Samuel 14:21
7529.text: And the Hebrews that had come to belong to the Phi·lisʹtines as formerly and that had gone up with them into the camp round about, even they too were for proving themselves to be with Israel who was with Saul and Jonʹa·than.

7530.label: 1 Samuel 14:22
7530.text: All the men of Israel also that were hidden in the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im heard that the Phi·lisʹtines had taken to flight, and they too went pursuing closely after them into the battle.

7531.label: 1 Samuel 14:23
7531.text: And Jehovah proceeded on that day to save Israel, and the battle itself passed over to Beth-aʹven.

7532.label: 1 Samuel 14:24
7532.text: And the men of Israel themselves were hard pressed on that day, and yet Saul put the people under the pledge of an oath, saying: “Cursed is the man that eats bread before the evening and until I have taken vengeance upon my enemies!” And none of the people tasted bread.

7533.label: 1 Samuel 14:25
7533.text: And all those of the land came into the woods, when honey happened to be over all the surface of the field.

7534.label: 1 Samuel 14:26
7534.text: When the people came into the woods, why, look! there was a dripping of honey, but there was no one putting his hand to his mouth, because the people were afraid of the oath.

7535.label: 1 Samuel 14:27
7535.text: As for Jonʹa·than, he had not been listening when his father put the people under an oath, so he stretched out the tip of the rod that was in his hand and dipped it into the honeycomb and drew his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes began to beam.

7536.label: 1 Samuel 14:28
7536.text: At this one of the people answered and said: “Your father solemnly put the people under oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man that eats bread today!’” (And the people began to get tired.)

7537.label: 1 Samuel 14:29
7537.text: However, Jonʹa·than said: “My father has brought ostracism upon the land. SEE, please, how my eyes have beamed because I tasted this little bit of honey.

7538.label: 1 Samuel 14:30
7538.text: How much more so if the people had but eaten today from the spoil of their enemies that they found! For now the slaughter upon the Phi·lisʹtines has not been great.”

7539.label: 1 Samuel 14:31
7539.text: And on that day they kept striking down the Phi·lisʹtines from Michʹmash to Aiʹja·lon, and the people got to be very tired.

7540.label: 1 Samuel 14:32
7540.text: And the people began darting greedily at the spoil and taking sheep and cattle and calves and slaughtering them on the earth, and the people fell to eating along with the blood.

7541.label: 1 Samuel 14:33
7541.text: So they told Saul, saying: “Look! The people are sinning against Jehovah by eating along with the blood.” At this he said: “YOU have dealt treacherously. First of all, roll a great stone to me.”

7542.label: 1 Samuel 14:34
7542.text: After that Saul said: “Scatter among the people, and YOU must say to them, ‘Bring near to me, each one of YOU, his bull and, each one, his sheep, and YOU must do the slaughtering in this place and the eating, and YOU must not sin against Jehovah by eating along with the blood.’” Accordingly all the people brought near each one his bull that was in his hand that night and did the slaughtering there.

7543.label: 1 Samuel 14:35
7543.text: And Saul proceeded to build an altar to Jehovah. With it he started altar building to Jehovah.

7544.label: 1 Samuel 14:36
7544.text: Later Saul said: “Let us go down after the Phi·lisʹtines by night and plunder them until the morning lightens up, and let us not leave a single one among them.” To this they said: “Anything that is good in your eyes do.” Then the priest said: “Let us approach here to the [true] God.”

7545.label: 1 Samuel 14:37
7545.text: And Saul began to inquire of God: “Shall I go down after the Phi·lisʹtines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?” And he did not answer him on that day.

7546.label: 1 Samuel 14:38
7546.text: So Saul said: “Come near here, all YOU keymen of the people, and ascertain and see in what way this sin has come to be today.

7547.label: 1 Samuel 14:39
7547.text: For as Jehovah, who is the Deliverer of Israel, is alive, even if it is in Jonʹa·than my son, yet he will positively die.” But there was no one answering him out of all the people.

7548.label: 1 Samuel 14:40
7548.text: And he went on to say to all Israel: “YOU yourselves will come to be on the one side, and I and Jonʹa·than my son—we will come to be on the other side.” At this the people said to Saul: “What is good in your eyes do.”

7549.label: 1 Samuel 14:41
7549.text: And Saul proceeded to say to Jehovah: “O God of Israel, do give Thumʹmim!” Then Jonʹa·than and Saul were taken, and the people themselves went out.

7550.label: 1 Samuel 14:42
7550.text: Saul now said: “CAST lots to decide between me and Jonʹa·than my son.” And Jonʹa·than got to be taken.

7551.label: 1 Samuel 14:43
7551.text: Then Saul said to Jonʹa·than: “Do tell me, What have you done?” So Jonʹa·than told him and said: “I did for a fact taste a little honey on the tip of the rod that is in my hand. Here I am! Let me die!”

7552.label: 1 Samuel 14:44
7552.text: At this Saul said: “Thus may God do and thus may he add to it, if you do not positively die, Jonʹa·than.”

7553.label: 1 Samuel 14:45
7553.text: But the people said to Saul: “Is Jonʹa·than to die, who has performed this great salvation in Israel? It is unthinkable! As Jehovah is alive, not as much as a single hair of his head will fall to the earth; for it was with God that he worked this day.” With that the people redeemed Jonʹa·than, and he did not die.

7554.label: 1 Samuel 14:46
7554.text: So Saul withdrew from following the Phi·lisʹtines, and the Phi·lisʹtines themselves went to their place.

7555.label: 1 Samuel 14:47
7555.text: And Saul himself took the kingship over Israel and went warring round about against all his enemies, against Moʹab and against the sons of Amʹmon and against Eʹdom and against the kings of Zoʹbah and against the Phi·lisʹtines; and wherever he would turn he administered condemnation.

7556.label: 1 Samuel 14:48
7556.text: And he went on acting valiantly and proceeded to strike down Amʹa·lek and to deliver Israel out of the hand of their pillager.

7557.label: 1 Samuel 14:49
7557.text: And the sons of Saul came to be Jonʹa·than and Ishʹvi and Malʹchi-shuʹa, and, as for the names of his two daughters, the name of the one born first was Meʹrab and the name of the younger one Miʹchal.

7558.label: 1 Samuel 14:50
7558.text: And the name of Saul’s wife was A·hinʹo·am the daughter of A·himʹa·az, and the name of the chief of his army was Abʹner the son of Ner, the uncle of Saul.

7559.label: 1 Samuel 14:51
7559.text: And Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abʹner was the son of A·biʹel.

7560.label: 1 Samuel 14:52
7560.text: And the warfare continued heavy against the Phi·lisʹtines all the days of Saul. When Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant person, he would gather him to himself.

7561.label: 1 Samuel 15:1
7561.text: Then Samuel said to Saul: “It was I whom Jehovah sent to anoint you as king over his people Israel, and now listen to the voice of the words of Jehovah.

7562.label: 1 Samuel 15:2
7562.text: This is what Jehovah of armies has said, ‘I must call to account what Amʹa·lek did to Israel when he set himself against him in the way while he was coming up out of Egypt.

7563.label: 1 Samuel 15:3
7563.text: Now go, and you must strike down Amʹa·lek and devote him to destruction with all that he has, and you must not have compassion upon him, and you must put them to death, man as well as woman, child as well as suckling, bull as well as sheep, camel as well as ass.’”

7564.label: 1 Samuel 15:4
7564.text: Accordingly Saul summoned the people and took the count of them in Te·laʹim, two hundred thousand men on foot and ten thousand men of Judah.

7565.label: 1 Samuel 15:5
7565.text: And Saul proceeded to come as far as the city of Amʹa·lek and to lie in ambush by the torrent valley.

7566.label: 1 Samuel 15:6
7566.text: Meanwhile Saul said to the Kenʹites: “GO, DEPART, GO DOWN from the midst of the A·malʹek·ites, that I may not sweep you away with them. As for you, you exercised loving-kindness with all the sons of Israel at the time of their coming up out of Egypt.” So the Kenʹites departed from the midst of Amʹa·lek.

7567.label: 1 Samuel 15:7
7567.text: After that Saul went striking down Amʹa·lek from Havʹi·lah as far as Shur, which is in front of Egypt.

7568.label: 1 Samuel 15:8
7568.text: And he got to catch Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek alive, and all the other people he devoted to destruction with the edge of the sword.

7569.label: 1 Samuel 15:9
7569.text: But Saul and the people had compassion upon Aʹgag and upon the best of the flock and the herd and the fat ones and upon the rams and upon all that was good, and they did not wish to devote them to destruction. As for all the goods that were despicable and rejected, these they devoted to destruction.

7570.label: 1 Samuel 15:10
7570.text: The word of Jehovah now came to Samuel, saying:

7571.label: 1 Samuel 15:11
7571.text: “I do regret that I have caused Saul to reign as king, because he has turned back from following me, and my words he has not carried out.” And it was distressing to Samuel, and he kept crying out to Jehovah all night long.

7572.label: 1 Samuel 15:12
7572.text: Then Samuel got up early to meet Saul in the morning. But report was made to Samuel, saying: “Saul came to Carʹmel, and, look! he was erecting a monument for himself, and he then turned around and went across and descended to Gilʹgal.”

7573.label: 1 Samuel 15:13
7573.text: At length Samuel came to Saul, and Saul began to say to him: “Blessed are you of Jehovah. I have carried out the word of Jehovah.”

7574.label: 1 Samuel 15:14
7574.text: But Samuel said: “Then what does this sound of the flock in my ears mean, and the sound of the herd that I am hearing?”

7575.label: 1 Samuel 15:15
7575.text: To this Saul said: “From the A·malʹek·ites they have brought them, because the people had compassion upon the best of the flock and of the herd, for the purpose of sacrificing to Jehovah your God; but what was left over we have devoted to destruction.”

7576.label: 1 Samuel 15:16
