7576.text: At this Samuel said to Saul: “Stop! And I will tell you what Jehovah spoke to me last night.” So he said to him: “Speak!”

7577.label: 1 Samuel 15:17
7577.text: And Samuel went on to say: “Was it not when you were little in your own eyes that you were head of the tribes of Israel, and Jehovah proceeded to anoint you as king over Israel?

7578.label: 1 Samuel 15:18
7578.text: Later Jehovah sent you on a mission and said, ‘Go, and you must devote the sinners, the A·malʹek·ites, to destruction, and you must fight against them until you will have exterminated them.’

7579.label: 1 Samuel 15:19
7579.text: So why is it you did not obey the voice of Jehovah but went darting greedily at the spoil and doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah?”

7580.label: 1 Samuel 15:20
7580.text: However, Saul said to Samuel: “But I have obeyed the voice of Jehovah in that I went on the mission on which Jehovah had sent me and I brought Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek, but Amʹa·lek I have devoted to destruction.

7581.label: 1 Samuel 15:21
7581.text: And the people went taking from the spoil sheep and cattle, the choicest of them as something devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to Jehovah your God in Gilʹgal.”

7582.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
7582.text: In turn Samuel said: “Does Jehovah have as much delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in obeying the voice of Jehovah? Look! To obey is better than a sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams;

7583.label: 1 Samuel 15:23
7583.text: for rebelliousness is the same as the sin of divination, and pushing ahead presumptuously the same as [using] uncanny power and teraphim. Since you have rejected the word of Jehovah, he accordingly rejects you from being king.”

7584.label: 1 Samuel 15:24
7584.text: Then Saul said to Samuel: “I have sinned; for I have overstepped the order of Jehovah and your words, because I feared the people and so obeyed their voice.

7585.label: 1 Samuel 15:25
7585.text: And now, please, pardon my sin and return with me that I may prostrate myself to Jehovah.”

7586.label: 1 Samuel 15:26
7586.text: But Samuel said to Saul: “I shall not return with you, for you have rejected the word of Jehovah, and Jehovah rejects you from continuing as king over Israel.”

7587.label: 1 Samuel 15:27
7587.text: As Samuel was turning about to go, he immediately grabbed hold of the skirt of his sleeveless coat, but it ripped away.

7588.label: 1 Samuel 15:28
7588.text: At this Samuel said to him: “Jehovah has ripped away the royal rule of Israel from off you today, and he will certainly give it to a fellowman of yours who is better than you.

7589.label: 1 Samuel 15:29
7589.text: And, besides, the Excellency of Israel will not prove false, and He will not feel regrets, for He is not an earthling man so as to feel regrets.”

7590.label: 1 Samuel 15:30
7590.text: At this he said: “I have sinned. Now honor me, please, in front of the older men of my people and in front of Israel and return with me, and I shall certainly prostrate myself to Jehovah your God.”

7591.label: 1 Samuel 15:31
7591.text: So Samuel returned behind Saul, and Saul proceeded to prostrate himself to Jehovah.

7592.label: 1 Samuel 15:32
7592.text: After that Samuel said: “BRING Aʹgag the king of Amʹa·lek near to me.” Then Aʹgag went to him reluctantly, and Aʹgag began to say to himself: “Truly the bitter experience of death has departed.”

7593.label: 1 Samuel 15:33
7593.text: However, Samuel said: “Just as your sword has bereaved women of children, in that way your mother will be most bereaved of children among women.” With that Samuel went hacking Aʹgag to pieces before Jehovah in Gilʹgal.

7594.label: 1 Samuel 15:34
7594.text: Samuel now went his way to Raʹmah, and Saul, for his part, went up to his own house at Gibʹe·ah of Saul.

7595.label: 1 Samuel 15:35
7595.text: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, because Samuel had gone into mourning for Saul. As for Jehovah, he regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

7596.label: 1 Samuel 16:1
7596.text: Eventually Jehovah said to Samuel: “For how long will you be mourning for Saul, while I, on the other hand, have rejected him from ruling as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I shall send you to Jesʹse the Bethʹle·hem·ite, because I have provided among his sons a king for myself.”

7597.label: 1 Samuel 16:2
7597.text: But Samuel said: “How can I go? Once Saul has heard of it he will certainly kill me.” And Jehovah went on to say: “A young cow of the herd you should take with you, and you must say, ‘To sacrifice to Jehovah is why I have come.’

7598.label: 1 Samuel 16:3
7598.text: And you must call Jesʹse to the sacrifice; and I, for my part, shall make known to you what you should do, and you must anoint for me the one whom I designate to you.”

7599.label: 1 Samuel 16:4
7599.text: And Samuel proceeded to do what Jehovah spoke. When he came to Bethʹle·hem the older men of the city began to tremble at meeting him, and so they said: “Does your coming mean peace?”

7600.label: 1 Samuel 16:5
7600.text: To this he said: “It means peace. To sacrifice to Jehovah is why I have come. Sanctify yourselves, and YOU must come with me to the sacrifice.” Then he sanctified Jesʹse and his sons, after which he called them to the sacrifice.

7601.label: 1 Samuel 16:6
7601.text: And it came about that, as they came in and he caught sight of E·liʹab, he at once said: “Surely his anointed one is before Jehovah.”

7602.label: 1 Samuel 16:7
7602.text: But Jehovah said to Samuel: “Do not look at his appearance and at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For not the way man sees [is the way God sees], because mere man sees what appears to the eyes; but as for Jehovah, he sees what the heart is.”

7603.label: 1 Samuel 16:8
7603.text: Then Jesʹse called A·binʹa·dab and had him pass before Samuel, but he said: “Neither has Jehovah chosen this one.”

7604.label: 1 Samuel 16:9
7604.text: Next Jesʹse had Shamʹmah pass by, but he said: “Neither has Jehovah chosen this one.”

7605.label: 1 Samuel 16:10
7605.text: So Jesʹse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel; still Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Jehovah has not chosen these.”

7606.label: 1 Samuel 16:11
7606.text: Finally Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Are these all the boys?” To this he said: “The youngest one has till now been left out, and, look! he is pasturing the sheep.” At that Samuel said to Jesʹse: “Do send and fetch him, because we shall not sit down to meal until his coming here.”

7607.label: 1 Samuel 16:12
7607.text: Accordingly he sent and had him come. Now he was ruddy, a young man with beautiful eyes and handsome in appearance. Then Jehovah said: “Get up, anoint him, for this is he!”

7608.label: 1 Samuel 16:13
7608.text: Accordingly Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the spirit of Jehovah began to be operative upon David from that day forward. Later Samuel rose and went his way to Raʹmah.

7609.label: 1 Samuel 16:14
7609.text: And the very spirit of Jehovah departed from Saul, and a bad spirit from Jehovah terrorized him.

7610.label: 1 Samuel 16:15
7610.text: And the servants of Saul began to say to him: “Here, now, God’s bad spirit is terrorizing you.

7611.label: 1 Samuel 16:16
7611.text: Let our lord, please, command your servants before you that they should look for a skilled man playing upon the harp. And it must occur that, when God’s bad spirit comes to be upon you, he will have to play with his hand, and it will certainly be well with you.”

7612.label: 1 Samuel 16:17
7612.text: So Saul said to his servants: “Provide me, please, a man doing well at playing, and YOU must bring him to me.”

7613.label: 1 Samuel 16:18
7613.text: And one of the attendants proceeded to answer and say: “Look! I have seen how a son of Jesʹse the Bethʹle·hem·ite is skilled at playing, and he is a valiant, mighty man and a man of war and an intelligent speaker and a well-formed man, and Jehovah is with him.”

7614.label: 1 Samuel 16:19
7614.text: Then Saul sent messengers to Jesʹse and said: “Do send to me David your son, who is with the flock.”

7615.label: 1 Samuel 16:20
7615.text: So Jesʹse took an ass, bread and a skin bottle of wine and a kid of the goats and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.

7616.label: 1 Samuel 16:21
7616.text: Thus David came to Saul and attended upon him; and he got to loving him very much, and he came to be his armor-bearer.

7617.label: 1 Samuel 16:22
7617.text: Consequently Saul sent to Jesʹse, saying: “Let David, please, keep attending upon me, for he has found favor in my eyes.”

7618.label: 1 Samuel 16:23
7618.text: And it occurred that, when God’s spirit came to be upon Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand; and there was relief for Saul and it was well with him, and the bad spirit departed from upon him.

7619.label: 1 Samuel 17:1
7619.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines went collecting their camps together for war. When they were collected together at Soʹcoh, which belongs to Judah, then they took up camping between Soʹcoh and A·zeʹkah, in Eʹphes-damʹmim.

7620.label: 1 Samuel 17:2
7620.text: As for Saul and the men of Israel, they collected themselves together and took up camping in the low plain of Eʹlah, and they went drawing up in battle formation to meet the Phi·lisʹtines.

7621.label: 1 Samuel 17:3
7621.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines were standing on the mountain on this side, and the Israelites were standing on the mountain on that side, with the valley between them.

7622.label: 1 Samuel 17:4
7622.text: And a champion began to go out from the camps of the Phi·lisʹtines, his name being Go·liʹath, from Gath, his height being six cubits and a span.

7623.label: 1 Samuel 17:5
7623.text: And there was a helmet of copper on his head, and he was clad with a coat of mail, of overlapping scales, and the weight of the coat of mail was five thousand shekels of copper.

7624.label: 1 Samuel 17:6
7624.text: And there were greaves of copper above his feet and a javelin of copper between his shoulders.

7625.label: 1 Samuel 17:7
7625.text: And the wooden shaft of his spear was like the beam of loom workers, and the blade of his spear was six hundred shekels of iron; and the bearer of the large shield was marching ahead of him.

7626.label: 1 Samuel 17:8
7626.text: Then he stood still and began to call to the battle lines of Israel and say to them: “Why do YOU come out to draw up in battle formation? Am I not the Phi·lisʹtine and YOU servants belonging to Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

7627.label: 1 Samuel 17:9
7627.text: If he is able to fight with me and he does strike me down, we must then become servants to YOU. But if I myself am a match for him and I do strike him down, YOU must also become servants to us, and YOU must serve us.”

7628.label: 1 Samuel 17:10
7628.text: And the Phi·lisʹtine went on to say: “I myself do taunt the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together!”

7629.label: 1 Samuel 17:11
7629.text: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Phi·lisʹtine, then they became terrified and were greatly afraid.

7630.label: 1 Samuel 17:12
7630.text: Now David was the son of this Ephʹrath·ite from Bethʹle·hem of Judah whose name was Jesʹse. And he had eight sons. And in the days of Saul the man was already old among men.

7631.label: 1 Samuel 17:13
7631.text: And the three oldest sons of Jesʹse proceeded to go. They went after Saul to the war, and the names of his three sons that went into the war were E·liʹab the firstborn, and his second son A·binʹa·dab and the third Shamʹmah.

7632.label: 1 Samuel 17:14
7632.text: And David was the youngest, and the three oldest themselves went after Saul.

7633.label: 1 Samuel 17:15
7633.text: And David was going and returning from Saul to tend the sheep of his father at Bethʹle·hem.

7634.label: 1 Samuel 17:16
7634.text: And the Phi·lisʹtine kept coming forward at early morning and at evening and taking his position for forty days.

7635.label: 1 Samuel 17:17
7635.text: Then Jesʹse said to David his son: “Take, please, to your brothers this eʹphah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers.

7636.label: 1 Samuel 17:18
7636.text: And these ten portions of milk you should bring to the chief of the thousand; also, you should look after your own brothers as regards their welfare, and a token from them you should take.”

7637.label: 1 Samuel 17:19
7637.text: Meantime, Saul and they and all the other men of Israel were in the low plain of Eʹlah, fighting against the Phi·lisʹtines.

7638.label: 1 Samuel 17:20
7638.text: Accordingly David got up early in the morning and left the sheep to the keeper’s charge and picked up and went just as Jesʹse had commanded him. When he came to the camp enclosure, the military forces were going out to the battle line, and they raised a shout for the battle.

7639.label: 1 Samuel 17:21
7639.text: And Israel and the Phi·lisʹtines began drawing up battle line to meet battle line.

7640.label: 1 Samuel 17:22
7640.text: Immediately David left the baggage from off him to the care of the keeper of the baggage and went running to the battle line. When he came, he began asking about the welfare of his brothers.

7641.label: 1 Samuel 17:23
7641.text: While he was speaking with them, why, here the champion, his name being Go·liʹath the Phi·lisʹtine from Gath, was coming up from the battle lines of the Phi·lisʹtines, and he began speaking the same words as before, and David got to listen in.

7642.label: 1 Samuel 17:24
7642.text: As for all the men of Israel, on their seeing the man, why, they went fleeing on account of him and were very much afraid.

7643.label: 1 Samuel 17:25
7643.text: And the men of Israel began to say: “Have YOU seen this man that is coming up? For it is to taunt Israel that he is coming up. And it must occur that, the man who strikes him down, the king will enrich him with great riches, and his own daughter he will give him, and the house of his father he will set free in Israel.”

7644.label: 1 Samuel 17:26
7644.text: And David began to say to the men that were standing close by him: “What will be done to the man that strikes down that Phi·lisʹtine over there and actually turns away reproach from upon Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Phi·lisʹtine that he has to taunt the battle lines of the living God?”

7645.label: 1 Samuel 17:27
7645.text: Then the people said to him the same words as before, saying: “This is the way it will be done to the man that strikes him down.”

7646.label: 1 Samuel 17:28
7646.text: And E·liʹab his oldest brother got to hear as he spoke to the men, and E·liʹab’s anger grew hot against David, so that he said: “Why is it that you have come down? And in whose charge did you leave those few sheep behind in the wilderness? I myself well know your presumptuousness and the badness of your heart, because you have come down for the purpose of seeing the battle.”

7647.label: 1 Samuel 17:29
7647.text: To this David said: “What have I done now? Was it not just a word?”

7648.label: 1 Samuel 17:30
7648.text: With that he turned about from beside him toward someone else and went saying the same word as before, and, in turn, the people gave him the same reply as formerly.

7649.label: 1 Samuel 17:31
7649.text: So the words that David spoke came to be heard, and they went telling them before Saul. Hence he fetched him.

7650.label: 1 Samuel 17:32
7650.text: And David proceeded to say to Saul: “Do not let the heart of any man collapse within him. Your servant himself will go and actually fight with this Phi·lisʹtine.”

7651.label: 1 Samuel 17:33
7651.text: But Saul said to David: “You are not able to go against this Phi·lisʹtine to fight with him, for you are but a boy, and he is a man of war from his boyhood.”

7652.label: 1 Samuel 17:34
7652.text: And David went on to say to Saul: “Your servant became a shepherd of his father among the flock, and there came a lion, and also a bear, and [each] carried off a sheep from the drove.

7653.label: 1 Samuel 17:35
7653.text: And I went out after it and struck it down and made the rescue from its mouth. When it began rising against me, I grabbed hold of its beard and struck it down and put it to death.

7654.label: 1 Samuel 17:36
7654.text: Both the lion and the bear your servant struck down; and this uncircumcised Phi·lisʹtine must become like one of them, for he has taunted the battle lines of the living God.”

7655.label: 1 Samuel 17:37
7655.text: Then David added: “Jehovah, who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he it is who will deliver me from the hand of this Phi·lisʹtine.” At this Saul said to David: “Go, and may Jehovah himself prove to be with you.”

7656.label: 1 Samuel 17:38
7656.text: Saul now went clothing David with his garments, and he put a copper helmet upon his head, after which he clothed him with a coat of mail.

7657.label: 1 Samuel 17:39
7657.text: Then David girded his sword on over his garments and undertook to go [but could not], because he had not tried them out. Finally David said to Saul: “I am unable to go in these things, for I have not tried them out.” So David removed them off him.

7658.label: 1 Samuel 17:40
7658.text: And he proceeded to take his staff in his hand and to choose for himself the five smoothest stones from the torrent valley and to place them in his shepherds’ bag that served him as a receptacle, and in his hand was his sling. And he began approaching the Phi·lisʹtine.

7659.label: 1 Samuel 17:41
7659.text: And the Phi·lisʹtine began to come, coming nearer and nearer to David, and the man carrying the large shield was ahead of him.

7660.label: 1 Samuel 17:42
7660.text: Now when the Phi·lisʹtine looked and saw David, he began despising him because he proved to be a boy and ruddy, of beautiful appearance.

7661.label: 1 Samuel 17:43
7661.text: So the Phi·lisʹtine said to David: “Am I a dog, so that you are coming to me with staves?” With that the Phi·lisʹtine called down evil upon David by his gods.

7662.label: 1 Samuel 17:44
7662.text: And the Phi·lisʹtine went on to say to David: “Just come to me, and I will give your flesh to the fowls of the heavens and to the beasts of the field.”

7663.label: 1 Samuel 17:45
7663.text: In turn David said to the Phi·lisʹtine: “You are coming to me with a sword and with a spear and with a javelin, but I am coming to you with the name of Jehovah of armies, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have taunted.

7664.label: 1 Samuel 17:46
7664.text: This day Jehovah will surrender you into my hand, and I shall certainly strike you down and remove your head off you; and I shall certainly give the carcasses of the camp of the Phi·lisʹtines this day to the fowls of the heavens and to the wild beasts of the earth; and people of all the earth will know that there exists a God belonging to Israel.

7665.label: 1 Samuel 17:47
7665.text: And all this congregation will know that neither with sword nor with spear does Jehovah save, because to Jehovah belongs the battle, and he must give YOU men into our hand.”

7666.label: 1 Samuel 17:48
7666.text: And it occurred that the Phi·lisʹtine rose and kept coming and drawing nearer to meet David, and David began hurrying and running toward the battle line to meet the Phi·lisʹtine.

7667.label: 1 Samuel 17:49
7667.text: Then David thrust his hand into his bag and took a stone from there and slung it, so that he struck the Phi·lisʹtine in his forehead and the stone sank into his forehead, and he went falling upon his face to the earth.

7668.label: 1 Samuel 17:50
7668.text: So David, with a sling and a stone, proved stronger than the Phi·lisʹtine and struck the Phi·lisʹtine down and put him to death; and there was no sword in David’s hand.

7669.label: 1 Samuel 17:51
7669.text: And David continued running and got to stand over the Phi·lisʹtine. Then he took his sword and pulled it out of its sheath and definitely put him to death when he cut his head off with it. And the Phi·lisʹtines got to see that their mighty one had died, and they took to flight.

7670.label: 1 Samuel 17:52
7670.text: At that the men of Israel and of Judah rose and broke into shouting and went in pursuit of the Phi·lisʹtines clear to [the] valley and as far as the gates of Ekʹron, and the fatally wounded of the Phi·lisʹtines kept falling on the way from Shaʹa·raʹim, both as far as Gath and as far as Ekʹron.

7671.label: 1 Samuel 17:53
7671.text: Afterward the sons of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Phi·lisʹtines and went pillaging their camps.

7672.label: 1 Samuel 17:54
7672.text: Then David took the head of the Phi·lisʹtine and brought it to Jerusalem, and his weapons he put in his tent.

7673.label: 1 Samuel 17:55
7673.text: Now at the moment that Saul saw David going out to meet the Phi·lisʹtine, he said to Abʹner the chief of the army: “Whose son is the boy, Abʹner?” To this Abʹner said: “By the life of your soul, O king, I do not know at all!”

7674.label: 1 Samuel 17:56
7674.text: So the king said: “You inquire whose son the lad is.”

7675.label: 1 Samuel 17:57
7675.text: Accordingly, as soon as David returned from striking the Phi·lisʹtine down, Abʹner proceeded to take him and bring him before Saul with the head of the Phi·lisʹtine in his hand.

7676.label: 1 Samuel 17:58
7676.text: Saul now said to him: “Whose son are you, boy?” to which David said: “The son of your servant Jesʹse the Bethʹle·hem·ite.”

7677.label: 1 Samuel 18:1
7677.text: And it came about that, as soon as he had finished speaking to Saul, Jonʹa·than’s very soul became bound up with the soul of David, and Jonʹa·than began to love him as his own soul.

7678.label: 1 Samuel 18:2
7678.text: Then Saul took him on that day, and he did not allow him to return to his father’s house.

7679.label: 1 Samuel 18:3
7679.text: And Jonʹa·than and David proceeded to conclude a covenant, because of his loving him as his own soul.

7680.label: 1 Samuel 18:4
7680.text: Further, Jonʹa·than stripped himself of the sleeveless coat that was on him and gave it to David, and also his garments, and even his sword and his bow and his belt.

7681.label: 1 Samuel 18:5
7681.text: And David began going out. Wherever Saul would send him he would act prudently, so that Saul placed him over the men of war; and it seemed good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of the servants of Saul.

7682.label: 1 Samuel 18:6
7682.text: And it came about that at their coming in, when David returned from striking the Phi·lisʹtines down, the women began coming out from all the cities of Israel with song and dances to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with rejoicing and with lutes.

7683.label: 1 Samuel 18:7
7683.text: And the women that were celebrating kept responding and saying: “Saul has struck down his thousands,And David his tens of thousands.”

7684.label: 1 Samuel 18:8
7684.text: And Saul began to be very angry, and this saying was bad from his viewpoint, so that he said: “They have given David tens of thousands, but to me they have given the thousands, and there is yet only the kingship to give him!”

7685.label: 1 Samuel 18:9
7685.text: And Saul was continually looking suspiciously at David from that day forward.

7686.label: 1 Samuel 18:10
7686.text: And it came about the next day that God’s bad spirit became operative upon Saul, so that he behaved like a prophet within the house, while David was playing music with his hand, as in former days; and the spear was in Saul’s hand.

7687.label: 1 Samuel 18:11
7687.text: And Saul proceeded to hurl the spear and say: “I will pin David even to the wall!” but David turned aside from before him, twice.

7688.label: 1 Samuel 18:12
7688.text: And Saul grew afraid of David because Jehovah proved to be with him, but from Saul he had departed.

7689.label: 1 Samuel 18:13
7689.text: Consequently Saul removed him from his company and appointed him as chief of a thousand for him; and he regularly went out and came in before the people.

7690.label: 1 Samuel 18:14
7690.text: And David was continually acting prudently in all his ways, and Jehovah was with him.

7691.label: 1 Samuel 18:15
7691.text: And Saul kept seeing that he was acting very prudently, so that he was scared of him.

7692.label: 1 Samuel 18:16
7692.text: And all Israel and Judah were lovers of David, because he was going out and coming in before them.

7693.label: 1 Samuel 18:17
7693.text: Finally Saul said to David: “Here is my oldest daughter Meʹrab. She is the one that I shall give you as a wife. Only prove yourself a valiant person to me and fight the wars of Jehovah.” But as for Saul, he said to himself: “Do not let my hand come to be upon him, but let the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines come to be upon him.”

7694.label: 1 Samuel 18:18
7694.text: At this David said to Saul: “Who am I and who are my kinsfolk, my father’s family, in Israel, so that I should become son-in-law to the king?”

7695.label: 1 Samuel 18:19
7695.text: However, it came about that at the time for giving Meʹrab, Saul’s daughter, to David, she herself had already been given to Aʹdri·el the Me·holʹath·ite as a wife.

7696.label: 1 Samuel 18:20
7696.text: Now Miʹchal, Saul’s daughter, was in love with David, and they went reporting it to Saul, and the matter was to his liking.

7697.label: 1 Samuel 18:21
7697.text: So Saul said: “I shall give her to him that she may serve as a snare to him, and that the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines may come to be upon him.” Accordingly Saul said to David: “By [one of] the two women you will form a marriage alliance with me today.”

7698.label: 1 Samuel 18:22
7698.text: Further, Saul commanded his servants: “Speak to David secretly, saying, ‘Look! The king has found delight in you, and all his servants themselves have fallen in love with you. So now form a marriage alliance with the king.’”

7699.label: 1 Samuel 18:23
7699.text: And the servants of Saul began to speak these words in the ears of David, but David said: “Is it an easy thing in YOUR eyes to form a marriage alliance with the king, when I am a man of little means and lightly esteemed?”

7700.label: 1 Samuel 18:24
7700.text: Then the servants of Saul reported to him, saying: “It was with words like these that David spoke.”

7701.label: 1 Samuel 18:25
7701.text: At that Saul said: “This is what YOU men will say to David, ‘The king has delight, not in marriage money, but in a hundred foreskins of the Phi·lisʹtines, to avenge himself on the enemies of the king.’” But as for Saul, he had schemed to have David fall by the hand of the Phi·lisʹtines.

7702.label: 1 Samuel 18:26
7702.text: So his servants reported these words to David, and the matter was to David’s liking, to form a marriage alliance with the king, and the days had not yet expired.

7703.label: 1 Samuel 18:27
7703.text: So David rose and he and his men went and struck down among the Phi·lisʹtines two hundred men, and David came bringing their foreskins and giving them in full number to the king, to form a marriage alliance with the king. In turn Saul gave him Miʹchal his daughter as a wife.

7704.label: 1 Samuel 18:28
7704.text: And Saul got to see and know that Jehovah was with David. As for Miʹchal, Saul’s daughter, she loved him.

7705.label: 1 Samuel 18:29
7705.text: And again Saul felt still more fear because of David, and Saul came to be an enemy of David always.

7706.label: 1 Samuel 18:30
7706.text: And the princes of the Phi·lisʹtines would go out, and it would happen that as often as they went out David acted most prudently of all the servants of Saul; and his name came to be very precious.

7707.label: 1 Samuel 19:1
7707.text: At length Saul spoke to Jonʹa·than his son and to all his servants of putting David to death.

7708.label: 1 Samuel 19:2
7708.text: As for Jonʹa·than, Saul’s son, he took great delight in David. So Jonʹa·than told David, saying: “Saul my father is seeking to have you put to death. And now be on your guard, please, in the morning, and you must dwell in secrecy and keep yourself hidden.

7709.label: 1 Samuel 19:3
7709.text: And I, for my part, shall go out and certainly stand at the side of my father in the field where you will be, and I myself shall speak for you to my father, and I shall certainly see what will happen, and I shall be sure to tell you.”

7710.label: 1 Samuel 19:4
7710.text: Accordingly Jonʹa·than spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him: “Do not let the king sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned toward you and his works have been very good toward you.

7711.label: 1 Samuel 19:5
7711.text: And he proceeded to put his soul in his palm and strike the Phi·lisʹtine down, so that Jehovah performed a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it, and you gave way to rejoicing. So why should you sin against innocent blood in having David put to death for nothing?”

7712.label: 1 Samuel 19:6
7712.text: Then Saul obeyed the voice of Jonʹa·than, and Saul swore: “As Jehovah is living, he will not be put to death.”

7713.label: 1 Samuel 19:7
7713.text: Afterward Jonʹa·than called David and Jonʹa·than told him all these words. Then Jonʹa·than brought David to Saul, and he continued before him the same as formerly.

7714.label: 1 Samuel 19:8
7714.text: In time war broke out again and David went sallying forth and fighting against the Phi·lisʹtines and striking them down with a great slaughter, and they took to flight from before him.

7715.label: 1 Samuel 19:9
7715.text: And Jehovah’s bad spirit came to be upon Saul when he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, while David was playing music with his hand.

7716.label: 1 Samuel 19:10
7716.text: Consequently Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he dodged from before Saul, so that he struck the spear into the wall. And David himself fled that he might escape during that night.

7717.label: 1 Samuel 19:11
7717.text: Later Saul sent messengers to David’s house to watch it and to have him put to death in the morning; but Miʹchal his wife told David, saying: “If you are not letting your soul escape tonight, tomorrow you will be a man put to death.”

7718.label: 1 Samuel 19:12
7718.text: Immediately Miʹchal had David descend through the window, that he might go and run away and escape.

7719.label: 1 Samuel 19:13
7719.text: Then Miʹchal took the teraphim image and placed it on the couch, and a net of goats’ hair she put at the place of his head, after which she covered it with a garment.

7720.label: 1 Samuel 19:14
7720.text: Saul now sent messengers to take David, but she said: “He is sick.”

7721.label: 1 Samuel 19:15
7721.text: So Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying: “Bring him on his couch up to me to have him put to death.”

7722.label: 1 Samuel 19:16
7722.text: When the messengers came in, why, there was the teraphim image on the couch and a net of goats’ hair at the place of his head.

7723.label: 1 Samuel 19:17
7723.text: At this Saul said to Miʹchal: “Why did you trick me like this, so that you sent my enemy away that he might escape?” In turn Miʹchal said to Saul: “He himself said to me, ‘Send me away! Why should I put you to death?’”

7724.label: 1 Samuel 19:18
7724.text: As for David, he ran away and made his escape and got to come to Samuel at Raʹmah. And he proceeded to tell him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went away, and they took up dwelling in Naiʹoth.

7725.label: 1 Samuel 19:19
7725.text: In time the report got to Saul, saying: “Look! David is in Naiʹoth in Raʹmah.”

7726.label: 1 Samuel 19:20
7726.text: At once Saul sent messengers to take David. When they got to see the elderly ones of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing in his position over them, the spirit of God came to be upon Saul’s messengers, and they began behaving like prophets, they also.

7727.label: 1 Samuel 19:21
7727.text: When they told it to Saul, he immediately sent other messengers, and they began behaving like prophets, they also. So Saul sent messengers again, the third set, and they began behaving like prophets, they also.

7728.label: 1 Samuel 19:22
7728.text: Finally he too went to Raʹmah. When he got as far as the great cistern that is in Seʹcu, he began to inquire and say: “Where are Samuel and David?” To this they said: “There in Naiʹoth in Raʹmah.”

7729.label: 1 Samuel 19:23
7729.text: And he kept on his way from there to Naiʹoth in Raʹmah, and the spirit of God came to be upon him, yes, him, and he went on walking and continued behaving like a prophet until he came into Naiʹoth in Raʹmah.

7730.label: 1 Samuel 19:24
7730.text: And he also proceeded to strip off his garments and behave, he also, like a prophet before Samuel, and he lay fallen naked all that day and all that night. That is why they came to say: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

7731.label: 1 Samuel 20:1
7731.text: And David went running away from Naiʹoth in Raʹmah. However, he came and said in front of Jonʹa·than: “What have I done? What is my error, and what sin have I committed before your father, for he is seeking for my soul?”

7732.label: 1 Samuel 20:2
7732.text: At this he said to him: “It is unthinkable! You will not die. Look! My father will not do a big thing or a little thing and not disclose it to my ear; and for what reason should my father conceal this matter from me? This does not happen.”

7733.label: 1 Samuel 20:3
7733.text: But David swore in addition and said: “Your father must surely know that I have found favor in your eyes, and so would say, ‘Do not let Jonʹa·than know this for fear he may feel hurt.’ But, in fact, as Jehovah is living and as your soul is living, there is just about a step between me and death!”

7734.label: 1 Samuel 20:4
7734.text: And Jonʹa·than went on to say to David: “Whatever your soul may say I shall do for you.”

7735.label: 1 Samuel 20:5
7735.text: At this David said to Jonʹa·than: “Look! Tomorrow is new moon, and I myself ought, without fail, to be sitting with the king to eat; and you must send me away, and I must conceal myself in the field until the evening on the third day.

7736.label: 1 Samuel 20:6
7736.text: If your father should miss me at all, then you must say, ‘David earnestly asked leave of absence of me to run to Bethʹle·hem his city, because there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.’

7737.label: 1 Samuel 20:7
7737.text: If the way he should say is, ‘It is all right!’ it means peace to your servant. But if he should at all become angry, know that what is bad has been determined upon by him.

7738.label: 1 Samuel 20:8
7738.text: And you must render loving-kindness toward your servant, for it is into a covenant of Jehovah that you have brought your servant with you. But if there is error in me, put me to death yourself, since why should it be to your father that you should bring me?”

7739.label: 1 Samuel 20:9
7739.text: To this Jonʹa·than said: “That is unthinkable respecting you! But if I should at all get to know that evil has been determined upon by my father to come upon you, shall I not tell it to you?”

7740.label: 1 Samuel 20:10
7740.text: Then David said to Jonʹa·than: “Who will tell me whether what your father may answer you is harsh?”

7741.label: 1 Samuel 20:11
7741.text: In turn Jonʹa·than said to David: “Just come, and let us go out into the field.” So both of them went out into the field.

7742.label: 1 Samuel 20:12
7742.text: And Jonʹa·than went on to say to David: “Jehovah the God of Israel [be a witness] that I shall sound out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and if he is well-disposed toward David, shall I not then send to you and certainly disclose it to your ear?

7743.label: 1 Samuel 20:13
7743.text: So may Jehovah do to Jonʹa·than and so may he add to it, if, in case it should seem good to my father to do evil against you, I do not indeed disclose it to your ear and send you away, and you do not certainly go in peace. And may Jehovah prove to be with you, just as he proved to be with my father.

7744.label: 1 Samuel 20:14
7744.text: And will you not, if I shall be still alive, yes, will you not exercise the loving-kindness of Jehovah toward me, that I may not die?

7745.label: 1 Samuel 20:15
7745.text: And you will not cut off your own loving-kindness from being with my household to time indefinite. Nor, when Jehovah cuts off the enemies of David, every one from the surface of the ground,

7746.label: 1 Samuel 20:16
7746.text: will [the name of] Jonʹa·than be cut off from the house of David. And Jehovah must require it at the hand of David’s enemies.”

7747.label: 1 Samuel 20:17
7747.text: So Jonʹa·than swore again to David because of his love for him; for as he loved his own soul he loved him.

7748.label: 1 Samuel 20:18
7748.text: And Jonʹa·than went on to say to him: “Tomorrow is new moon, and you will certainly be missed, because your seat will be vacant.

7749.label: 1 Samuel 20:19
7749.text: And certainly on the third day you will be missed very much; and you must come to the place where you concealed yourself on the working day, and you must dwell near this stone here.

7750.label: 1 Samuel 20:20
7750.text: And as for me, I shall shoot three arrows to one side of it, to send them where I will to a target.

7751.label: 1 Samuel 20:21
7751.text: And, look! I shall send the attendant, [saying,] ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I should specifically say to the attendant, ‘Look! The arrows are on this side of you, take them,’ then you come, for it means peace for you and there is nothing the matter, as Jehovah is living.

7752.label: 1 Samuel 20:22
7752.text: But if this is the way I should say to the lad, ‘Look! The arrows are farther away from you,’ go, for Jehovah has sent you away.

7753.label: 1 Samuel 20:23
7753.text: And as for the word that we have spoken, I and you, why, may Jehovah be between me and you to time indefinite.”

7754.label: 1 Samuel 20:24
7754.text: And David proceeded to conceal himself in the field. And it came to be new moon, and the king took his seat at the meal to eat.

7755.label: 1 Samuel 20:25
7755.text: And the king was sitting in his seat as at other times, in the seat by the wall; and Jonʹa·than was facing him, and Abʹner was sitting at Saul’s side, but David’s place was vacant.

7756.label: 1 Samuel 20:26
7756.text: And Saul did not say anything at all on that day, for he said to himself: “Something has happened so that he is not clean, for he has not been cleansed.”

7757.label: 1 Samuel 20:27
7757.text: And it came about the day after the new moon, on the second day, that David’s place continued vacant. At this Saul said to Jonʹa·than his son: “Why has not the son of Jesʹse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”

7758.label: 1 Samuel 20:28
7758.text: So Jonʹa·than answered Saul: “David earnestly asked leave of absence from me [to go] to Bethʹle·hem.

7759.label: 1 Samuel 20:29
7759.text: And he went on to say, ‘Send me away, please, because we have a family sacrifice in the city, and it was my own brother that commanded me. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me slip away, please, that I may see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.”

7760.label: 1 Samuel 20:30
7760.text: Then Saul’s anger grew hot against Jonʹa·than and he said to him: “You son of a rebellious maid, do I not well know that you are choosing the son of Jesʹse to your own shame and to the shame of the secret parts of your mother?

7761.label: 1 Samuel 20:31
7761.text: For all the days that the son of Jesʹse is alive on the ground, you and your kingship will not be firmly established. So now send and fetch him to me, for he is destined for death.”

7762.label: 1 Samuel 20:32
7762.text: However, Jonʹa·than answered Saul his father and said to him: “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”

7763.label: 1 Samuel 20:33
7763.text: At that Saul went hurling the spear at him to strike him; and Jonʹa·than came to know that it had been determined upon by his father to put David to death.

7764.label: 1 Samuel 20:34
7764.text: Immediately Jonʹa·than rose up from the table in the heat of anger, and he did not eat bread on the second day after the new moon, for he had been hurt respecting David, because his own father had humiliated him.

7765.label: 1 Samuel 20:35
7765.text: And it came about in the morning that Jonʹa·than made his way out to the field of David’s appointed place, and a young attendant was with him.

7766.label: 1 Samuel 20:36
7766.text: And he proceeded to say to his attendant: “Run, please, find the arrows that I am shooting.” The attendant ran, and he himself shot the arrow to make it pass beyond him.

7767.label: 1 Samuel 20:37
7767.text: When the attendant came as far as the place of the arrow that Jonʹa·than had shot, Jonʹa·than began to call from behind the attendant and say: “Is not the arrow farther away from you?”

7768.label: 1 Samuel 20:38
7768.text: And Jonʹa·than went on calling from behind the attendant: “In haste! Act quickly! Do not stand still!” And the attendant of Jonʹa·than went picking up the arrows and then came to his master.

7769.label: 1 Samuel 20:39
7769.text: As for the attendant, he did not know anything; only Jonʹa·than and David themselves knew about the matter.

7770.label: 1 Samuel 20:40
7770.text: After that Jonʹa·than gave his weapons to the attendant that belonged to him and he said to him: “Go, take them to the city.”

7771.label: 1 Samuel 20:41
7771.text: The attendant went. As for David, he rose up from nearby to the south. Then he fell on his face to the earth and bowed three times; and they began kissing each other and weeping for each other, until David had done it the most.

7772.label: 1 Samuel 20:42
7772.text: And Jonʹa·than went on to say to David: “Go in peace, since we have sworn, both of us, in the name of Jehovah, saying, ‘May Jehovah himself prove to be between me and you and between my offspring and your offspring to time indefinite.’” Accordingly David rose up and went his way, and Jonʹa·than himself came into the city.

7773.label: 1 Samuel 21:1
7773.text: Later David came into Nob to A·himʹe·lech the priest; and A·himʹe·lech began to tremble at meeting David and then said to him: “Why is it you are by yourself, and no one is with you?”

7774.label: 1 Samuel 21:2
7774.text: At this David said to A·himʹe·lech the priest: “The king himself commanded me as to a matter, and he went on to say to me, ‘Let no one know anything at all of the matter concerning which I am sending you and concerning which I have commanded you.’ And I have made an appointment with the young men for such and such a place.

7775.label: 1 Samuel 21:3
7775.text: And now, if there are five loaves of bread at your disposal, just give them into my hand, or whatever may be found.”

7776.label: 1 Samuel 21:4
7776.text: But the priest answered David and said: “There is no ordinary bread under my hand, but there is holy bread; provided that the young men have at least kept themselves from womankind.”

7777.label: 1 Samuel 21:5
7777.text: So David answered the priest and said to him: “But womankind has been kept away from us the same as formerly when I went out, and the organisms of the young men continue holy, although the mission itself is ordinary. And how much more so today, when one becomes holy in [his] organism?”

7778.label: 1 Samuel 21:6
7778.text: At that the priest gave him what was holy, because there happened to be no bread there but the showbread that had been removed from before Jehovah so as to place fresh bread there on the day of its being taken away.

7779.label: 1 Samuel 21:7
7779.text: Now one of Saul’s servants was there on that day, detained before Jehovah, and his name was Doʹeg the Eʹdom·ite, the principal one of the shepherds that belonged to Saul.

7780.label: 1 Samuel 21:8
7780.text: And David went on to say to A·himʹe·lech: “And is there nothing here at your disposal, a spear or a sword? For neither my own sword nor my weapons did I take in my hand, because the king’s matter proved to be urgent.”

7781.label: 1 Samuel 21:9
7781.text: To this the priest said: “The sword of Go·liʹath the Phi·lisʹtine, whom you struck down in the low plain of Eʹlah —here it is, wrapped up in a mantle, behind the ephʹod. If it is what you would take for yourself, take it, because there is no other here except it.” And David went on to say: “There is none like it. Give it to me.”

7782.label: 1 Samuel 21:10
7782.text: Then David rose up and continued running away on account of Saul on that day, and at length came to Aʹchish the king of Gath.

7783.label: 1 Samuel 21:11
7783.text: And the servants of Aʹchish began to say to him: “Is not this David the king of the land? Was it not to this one that they kept responding with dances, saying,‘Saul has struck down his thousands,And David his tens of thousands’?”

7784.label: 1 Samuel 21:12
7784.text: And David began to take these words to his heart, and he became very much afraid on account of Aʹchish the king of Gath.

7785.label: 1 Samuel 21:13
7785.text: So he disguised his sanity under their eyes and began acting insane in their hand and kept making cross marks on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down upon his beard.

7786.label: 1 Samuel 21:14
7786.text: Finally Aʹchish said to his servants: “Here YOU see a man behaving crazy. Why should YOU bring him to me?

7787.label: 1 Samuel 21:15
7787.text: Am I in need of people driven crazy, so that YOU have brought this one to behave crazy by me? Should this one come into my home?”

7788.label: 1 Samuel 22:1
7788.text: So David proceeded to go from there and escape to the cave of A·dulʹlam; and his brothers and the entire house of his father got to hear of it and made their way down there to him.

7789.label: 1 Samuel 22:2
7789.text: And all men in distress and all men who had a creditor and all men bitter in soul began to collect together to him, and he came to be a chief over them; and there came to be with him about four hundred men.

7790.label: 1 Samuel 22:3
7790.text: Later David went from there to Mizʹpeh in Moʹab and said to the king of Moʹab: “Let my father and my mother, please, dwell with YOU people until I know what God will do to me.”

7791.label: 1 Samuel 22:4
7791.text: Accordingly he settled them before the king of Moʹab, and they continued dwelling with him all the days that David happened to be in the inaccessible place.

7792.label: 1 Samuel 22:5
7792.text: In time Gad the prophet said to David: “You must not keep dwelling in the inaccessible place. Go away, and you must come yourself into the land of Judah.” Hence David went away and came into the forest of Heʹreth.

7793.label: 1 Samuel 22:6
7793.text: And Saul got to hear that David and the men that were with him had been discovered, while Saul was sitting in Gibʹe·ah under the tamarisk tree on the high place with his spear in his hand and all his servants stationed about him.

7794.label: 1 Samuel 22:7
7794.text: Then Saul said to his servants stationed about him: “Listen, please, YOU Benʹja·min·ites. Will the son of Jesʹse also give to all of YOU fields and vineyards? Will he appoint all of YOU chiefs of thousands and chiefs of hundreds?

7795.label: 1 Samuel 22:8
7795.text: For YOU have conspired, all of YOU, against me; and there is no one disclosing it to my ear when my own son concludes [a covenant] with the son of Jesʹse, and there is no one of YOU having sympathy for me and disclosing to my ear that my own son has raised up my own servant against me as a lier in ambush the way it is this day.”

7796.label: 1 Samuel 22:9
7796.text: At this Doʹeg the Eʹdom·ite, being stationed as he was over the servants of Saul, answered and said: “I saw the son of Jesʹse come to Nob to A·himʹe·lech the son of A·hiʹtub.

7797.label: 1 Samuel 22:10
7797.text: And he proceeded to inquire of Jehovah for him; and provisions he gave him, and the sword of Go·liʹath the Phi·lisʹtine he gave him.”

7798.label: 1 Samuel 22:11
7798.text: At once the king sent to call A·himʹe·lech the son of A·hiʹtub the priest and all the house of his father, the priests that were in Nob. So all of them came to the king.

7799.label: 1 Samuel 22:12
7799.text: Saul now said: “Listen, please, you son of A·hiʹtub!” to which he said: “Here I am, my lord.”

7800.label: 1 Samuel 22:13
7800.text: And Saul went on to say to him: “Why have YOU men conspired against me, you and the son of Jesʹse, by your giving him bread and a sword, and there being an inquiry of God for him, to rise up against me as a lier in ambush the way it is this day?”

7801.label: 1 Samuel 22:14
7801.text: At this A·himʹe·lech answered the king and said: “And who among all your servants is like David, faithful, and the son-in-law of the king and a chief over your bodyguard and honored in your house?

7802.label: 1 Samuel 22:15
7802.text: Is it today that I have started to inquire of God for him? It is unthinkable on my part! Do not let the king lay anything against his servant [and] against the entire house of my father, for in all this your servant did not know a thing small or great.”

7803.label: 1 Samuel 22:16
7803.text: But the king said: “You will positively die, A·himʹe·lech, you with all the house of your father.”

7804.label: 1 Samuel 22:17
7804.text: With that the king said to the runners stationed about him: “Turn and put to death the priests of Jehovah, because their hand also is with David and because they knew that he was a runaway and they did not disclose it to my ear!” And the servants of the king did not want to thrust out their hand to assault the priests of Jehovah.

7805.label: 1 Samuel 22:18
7805.text: Finally the king said to Doʹeg: “You turn and assault the priests!” Immediately Doʹeg the Eʹdom·ite turned and himself assaulted the priests and put to death on that day eighty-five men bearing an ephʹod of linen.

7806.label: 1 Samuel 22:19
7806.text: Even Nob the city of the priests he struck with the edge of the sword, man as well as woman, child as well as suckling and bull and ass and sheep with the edge of the sword.

7807.label: 1 Samuel 22:20
7807.text: However, one son of A·himʹe·lech the son of A·hiʹtub, whose name was A·biʹa·thar, made his escape and went running away to follow David.

7808.label: 1 Samuel 22:21
7808.text: Then A·biʹa·thar told David: “Saul has killed the priests of Jehovah.”

7809.label: 1 Samuel 22:22
7809.text: At this David said to A·biʹa·thar: “I well knew on that day, because Doʹeg the Eʹdom·ite was there, that he would without fail tell Saul. I personally have wronged every soul of the house of your father.

7810.label: 1 Samuel 22:23
7810.text: Just dwell with me. Do not be afraid, for whoever looks for my soul looks for your soul, for you are one needing protection with me.”

7811.label: 1 Samuel 23:1
7811.text: In time they came reporting to David, saying: “Here the Phi·lisʹtines are warring against Keiʹlah, and they are pillaging the threshing floors.”

7812.label: 1 Samuel 23:2
7812.text: And David proceeded to inquire of Jehovah, saying: “Shall I go, and must I strike down these Phi·lisʹtines?” In turn Jehovah said to David: “Go, and you must strike down the Phi·lisʹtines and save Keiʹlah.”

7813.label: 1 Samuel 23:3
7813.text: At this the men of David said to him: “Look! We are afraid while here in Judah, and how much more so in case we should go to Keiʹlah against the battle lines of the Phi·lisʹtines!”

7814.label: 1 Samuel 23:4
7814.text: So David inquired yet again of Jehovah. Jehovah now answered him and said: “Rise up, go down to Keiʹlah, because I am giving the Phi·lisʹtines into your hand.”

7815.label: 1 Samuel 23:5
7815.text: Accordingly David went with his men to Keiʹlah and fought against the Phi·lisʹtines and drove off with their livestock, but struck them down with a great slaughter; and David came to be the savior of the inhabitants of Keiʹlah.

7816.label: 1 Samuel 23:6
7816.text: Now it came about that when A·biʹa·thar the son of A·himʹe·lech ran away to David at Keiʹlah, there was an ephʹod that went down in his hand.

7817.label: 1 Samuel 23:7
7817.text: In time the report was made to Saul: “David has come to Keiʹlah.” And Saul began to say: “God has sold him into my hand, for he has shut himself up by coming into a city with doors and bar.”

7818.label: 1 Samuel 23:8
7818.text: So Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keiʹlah, to besiege David and his men.

7819.label: 1 Samuel 23:9
7819.text: And David got to know that Saul was fabricating mischief against him. Hence he said to A·biʹa·thar the priest: “Do bring the ephʹod near.”

7820.label: 1 Samuel 23:10
7820.text: And David went on to say: “O Jehovah the God of Israel, your servant has definitely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keiʹlah to lay the city in ruin on my account.

7821.label: 1 Samuel 23:11
7821.text: Will the landowners of Keiʹlah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down just as your servant has heard? O Jehovah the God of Israel, tell your servant, please.” To this Jehovah said: “He will come down.”

7822.label: 1 Samuel 23:12
7822.text: And David went on to say: “Will the landowners of Keiʹlah surrender me and my men into Saul’s hand?” In turn Jehovah said: “They will do the surrendering.”

7823.label: 1 Samuel 23:13
7823.text: At once David rose up with his men, about six hundred men, and they went out of Keiʹlah and continued walking about wherever they could walk about. And to Saul it was reported that David had escaped from Keiʹlah, and so he gave up going out.

7824.label: 1 Samuel 23:14
7824.text: And David took up dwelling in the wilderness in places difficult to approach, and he kept dwelling in the mountainous region in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul kept looking for him always, and God did not give him into his hand.

7825.label: 1 Samuel 23:15
7825.text: And David continued in fear because Saul had gone out to look for his soul while David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Hoʹresh.

7826.label: 1 Samuel 23:16
7826.text: Jonʹa·than the son of Saul now rose up and went to David at Hoʹresh, that he might strengthen his hand in regard to God.

7827.label: 1 Samuel 23:17
7827.text: And he went on to say to him: “Do not be afraid; for the hand of Saul my father will not find you, and you yourself will be king over Israel, and I myself shall become second to you; and Saul my father also has knowledge to that effect.”

7828.label: 1 Samuel 23:18
7828.text: Then the two of them concluded a covenant before Jehovah; and David kept dwelling in Hoʹresh, and Jonʹa·than himself went to his own home.

7829.label: 1 Samuel 23:19
7829.text: Later the men of Ziph went up to Saul at Gibʹe·ah, saying: “Is not David concealing himself close by us in the places difficult to approach at Hoʹresh, on the hill of Hach·iʹlah, which is to the right side of Je·shiʹmon?

7830.label: 1 Samuel 23:20
7830.text: And now in harmony with all the craving of your soul, O king, to come down, come down, and our part will be to surrender him into the hand of the king.”

7831.label: 1 Samuel 23:21
7831.text: At this Saul said: “Blessed are YOU of Jehovah, for YOU have had compassion on me.

7832.label: 1 Samuel 23:22
7832.text: Go, please, persevere some more and ascertain and see his place where his foot comes to be—whoever saw him there—for it has been said to me that he himself is surely cunning.

7833.label: 1 Samuel 23:23
7833.text: And see and ascertain about all the hiding places where he hides himself; and YOU must return to me with the evidence, and I will go with YOU; and it must occur that, if he is in the land, I will also search for him carefully among all the thousands of Judah.”

7834.label: 1 Samuel 23:24
7834.text: So they rose up and went to Ziph ahead of Saul, while David and his men were in the wilderness of Maʹon in the Arʹa·bah to the south of Je·shiʹmon.

7835.label: 1 Samuel 23:25
7835.text: Later Saul came with his men to look for him. When they told David, he at once went down to the crag and continued dwelling in the wilderness of Maʹon. When Saul got to hear of it, he went chasing after David into the wilderness of Maʹon.

7836.label: 1 Samuel 23:26
7836.text: Eventually Saul came to this side of the mountain, and David and his men were on that side of the mountain. So David became hurried to go away because of Saul; all the while Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to grab hold of them.

7837.label: 1 Samuel 23:27
7837.text: But there was a messenger that came to Saul, saying: “Do hasten and go, for the Phi·lisʹtines have made a raid on the land!”

7838.label: 1 Samuel 23:28
7838.text: At that Saul turned back from chasing after David and went to meet the Phi·lisʹtines. That is why they have called that place the Crag of the Divisions.

7839.label: 1 Samuel 23:29
7839.text: Then David made his way up from there and took up dwelling in the places difficult to approach at En-geʹdi.

7840.label: 1 Samuel 24:1
7840.text: And it came about that, as soon as Saul returned from following the Phi·lisʹtines, they came reporting to him, saying: “Look! David is in the wilderness of En-geʹdi.”

7841.label: 1 Samuel 24:2
7841.text: And Saul proceeded to take three thousand chosen men out of all Israel and to go looking for David and his men upon the bare rocks of the mountain goats.

7842.label: 1 Samuel 24:3
7842.text: At length he came to the stone sheepfolds along the road, where a cave was. So Saul came in to ease nature, while David and his men were in the parts of the cave farthest back, sitting down.

7843.label: 1 Samuel 24:4
7843.text: And David’s men began to say to him: “Here is the day on which Jehovah does say to you, ‘Look! I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you must do to him just as it may seem good in your eyes.’” So David rose up and quietly cut off the skirt of the sleeveless coat that belonged to Saul.

7844.label: 1 Samuel 24:5
7844.text: But it came about afterward that David’s heart kept striking him for the reason that he had cut off the skirt [of the sleeveless coat] that belonged to Saul.

7845.label: 1 Samuel 24:6
7845.text: Hence he said to his men: “It is unthinkable, on my part, from Jehovah’s standpoint, that I should do this thing to my lord, the anointed of Jehovah, by thrusting out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of Jehovah.”

7846.label: 1 Samuel 24:7
7846.text: Accordingly David dispersed his men with these words, and he did not allow them to rise up against Saul. As for Saul, he rose up from the cave and kept going on his way.

7847.label: 1 Samuel 24:8
7847.text: So David rose up afterward and went out from the cave and called out after Saul, saying: “My lord the king!” At this Saul looked behind him, and David proceeded to bow low with his face to the earth and prostrate himself.

7848.label: 1 Samuel 24:9
7848.text: And David went on to say to Saul: “Why do you listen to the words of man, saying, ‘Look! David is seeking your hurt’?

7849.label: 1 Samuel 24:10
7849.text: Here this day your eyes have seen how Jehovah gave you today into my hand in the cave; and someone said to kill you, but I felt sorry for you and said, ‘I shall not thrust out my hand against my lord, for he is the anointed of Jehovah.’

7850.label: 1 Samuel 24:11
7850.text: And, my father, see, yes, see the skirt of your sleeveless coat in my hand, for when I cut off the skirt of your sleeveless coat I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no badness or revolt in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, while you are lying in wait for my soul to take it away.

7851.label: 1 Samuel 24:12
7851.text: May Jehovah judge between me and you; and Jehovah must take vengeance for me from you, but my own hand will not come to be upon you.

7852.label: 1 Samuel 24:13
7852.text: Just as the proverb of the ancients says, ‘From the wicked ones wickedness will go forth,’ but my own hand will not come to be upon you.

7853.label: 1 Samuel 24:14
7853.text: After whom has the king of Israel gone out? After whom are you chasing? After a dead dog? After a single flea?

7854.label: 1 Samuel 24:15
7854.text: And Jehovah must become judge, and he must judge between me and you, and he will see and he will conduct the legal case for me and judge me [to free me] from your hand.”

7855.label: 1 Samuel 24:16
7855.text: And it came about that, at the moment that David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul proceeded to say: “Is this your voice, my son David?” And Saul began to raise his own voice and weep.

7856.label: 1 Samuel 24:17
7856.text: And he went on to say to David: “You are more righteous than I am, for it is you who have rendered me good, and it is I who have rendered you evil.

7857.label: 1 Samuel 24:18
7857.text: And you—you have told today what good you have done in connection with me in that Jehovah surrendered me into your hand and you did not kill me.

7858.label: 1 Samuel 24:19
7858.text: Now in the case where a man finds his enemy, will he send him away on a good road? So Jehovah himself will reward you with good, due to the fact that this day you have done it to me.

7859.label: 1 Samuel 24:20
7859.text: And now, look! I well know that you will, without fail, rule as king, and that in your hand the kingdom of Israel will certainly endure.

7860.label: 1 Samuel 24:21
7860.text: So now do swear to me by Jehovah that you will not cut off my seed after me and that you will not annihilate my name out of the house of my father.”

7861.label: 1 Samuel 24:22
7861.text: Accordingly David swore to Saul, after which Saul went to his home. As for David and his men, they went up to the place difficult to approach.

7862.label: 1 Samuel 25:1
7862.text: In time Samuel died; and all Israel proceeded to collect together and bewail him and bury him at his house in Raʹmah. Then David rose up and went down to the wilderness of Paʹran.

7863.label: 1 Samuel 25:2
7863.text: Now there was a man in Maʹon, and his work was in Carʹmel. And the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and he came to be [engaged] in shearing his sheep at Carʹmel.

7864.label: 1 Samuel 25:3
7864.text: And the man’s name was Naʹbal, and his wife’s name was Abʹi·gail. And the wife was good in discretion and beautiful in form, but the husband was harsh and bad in his practices; and he was a Caʹleb·ite.

7865.label: 1 Samuel 25:4
7865.text: And David got to hear in the wilderness that Naʹbal was shearing his sheep.

7866.label: 1 Samuel 25:5
7866.text: So David sent ten young men and David said to the young men: “Go up to Carʹmel, and YOU must come to Naʹbal and ask him in my name about his welfare.

7867.label: 1 Samuel 25:6
7867.text: And this is what YOU must say to my brother, ‘May you be well and also your household be well and all that you have be well.

7868.label: 1 Samuel 25:7
7868.text: And now I have heard that you have shearers. Now the shepherds that belong to you happened themselves to be with us. We did not molest them, and nothing at all showed up missing of theirs all the days they happened to be in Carʹmel.

7869.label: 1 Samuel 25:8
7869.text: Ask your own young men, and they will tell you, that my young men may find favor in your eyes, because it was upon a good day that we came. Just give, please, whatever your hand may find to your servants and to your son David.’”

7870.label: 1 Samuel 25:9
7870.text: Accordingly David’s young men came and spoke to Naʹbal in accord with all these words in the name of David and then waited.

7871.label: 1 Samuel 25:10
7871.text: At this Naʹbal answered David’s servants and said: “Who is David, and who is the son of Jesʹse? Nowadays the servants that are breaking away, each one from before his master, have become many.

7872.label: 1 Samuel 25:11
7872.text: And do I have to take my bread and my water and my slaughtered meat that I have butchered for my shearers and give it to men of whom I do not even know from where they are?”

7873.label: 1 Samuel 25:12
7873.text: Upon that David’s young men turned around on their way and went back and came and reported to him in accord with all these words.

7874.label: 1 Samuel 25:13
7874.text: Immediately David said to his men: “Gird on every one his sword!” So they girded on every one his sword and David also girded on his own sword; and they began to go up after David, about four hundred men, while two hundred sat by the baggage.

7875.label: 1 Samuel 25:14
7875.text: Meanwhile, to Abʹi·gail, Naʹbal’s wife, one of the young men reported, saying: “Look! David sent messengers from the wilderness to wish our master well, but he screamed rebukes at them.

7876.label: 1 Samuel 25:15
7876.text: And the men were very good to us, and they did not molest us, and we did not miss a single thing all the days of our walking about with them while we happened to be in the field.

7877.label: 1 Samuel 25:16
7877.text: A wall was what they proved to be around us both by night and by day, all the days that we happened to be with them, shepherding the flock.

7878.label: 1 Samuel 25:17
7878.text: And now know and see what you are going to do, for calamity has been determined against our master and against all his house, as he is too much of a good-for-nothing fellow to speak to him.”

7879.label: 1 Samuel 25:18
7879.text: At once Abʹi·gail hastened and took two hundred loaves of bread and two large jars of wine and five sheep dressed and five seah measures of roasted grain and a hundred cakes of raisins and two hundred cakes of pressed figs and put them upon the asses.

7880.label: 1 Samuel 25:19
7880.text: Then she said to her young men: “Pass on ahead of me. Look! I am coming after YOU.” But to her husband Naʹbal she told nothing.

7881.label: 1 Samuel 25:20
7881.text: And it occurred that while she was riding on the ass and secretly going down the mountain, why, there were David and his men coming down to meet her. So she encountered them.

7882.label: 1 Samuel 25:21
7882.text: As for David, he had said: “It was altogether for disappointment that I guarded everything that belongs to this fellow in the wilderness and not a single thing of all that belongs to him showed up missing, and yet he repays me evil in return for good.

7883.label: 1 Samuel 25:22
7883.text: So may God do to the enemies of David and so may he add to it if I shall let anyone of all who are his that urinates against the wall remain until the morning.”

7884.label: 1 Samuel 25:23
7884.text: When Abʹi·gail caught sight of David, she at once hastened and got down off the ass and fell upon her face before David and bowed to the earth.

7885.label: 1 Samuel 25:24
7885.text: She then fell at his feet and said: “Upon me myself, O my lord, be the error; and, please, let your slave girl speak in your ears, and listen to the words of your slave girl.

7886.label: 1 Samuel 25:25
7886.text: Please, do not let my lord set his heart upon this good-for-nothing man Naʹbal, for, as his name is, so is he. Naʹbal is his name, and senselessness is with him. As for me your slave girl, I did not see my lord’s young men that you had sent.

7887.label: 1 Samuel 25:26
7887.text: And now, my lord, as Jehovah is living and as your soul is living, Jehovah has held you back from entering into bloodguilt and having your own hand come to your salvation. And now let your enemies and those seeking injury to my lord become like Naʹbal.

7888.label: 1 Samuel 25:27
7888.text: And now as regards this gift blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord, it must be given to the young men that are walking about in the steps of my lord.

7889.label: 1 Samuel 25:28
7889.text: Pardon, please, the transgression of your slave girl, because Jehovah will without fail make for my lord a lasting house, because the wars of Jehovah are what my lord is fighting; and as for badness, it will not be found in you throughout your days.

7890.label: 1 Samuel 25:29
7890.text: When man rises up to pursue you and look for your soul, the soul of my lord will certainly prove to be wrapped up in the bag of life with Jehovah your God; but, as for the soul of your enemies, he will sling it forth as from inside the hollow of the sling.

7891.label: 1 Samuel 25:30
7891.text: And it must occur that, because Jehovah will do to my lord the good toward you according to all that he has spoken, he certainly will commission you as leader over Israel.

7892.label: 1 Samuel 25:31
7892.text: And let this not become to you a cause for staggering or a stumbling block to the heart of my lord, both by the shedding of blood without cause and by having [the hand of] my lord [itself] come to his salvation. And Jehovah will certainly do good to my lord, and you must remember your slave girl.”

7893.label: 1 Samuel 25:32
7893.text: At this David said to Abʹi·gail: “Blessed be Jehovah the God of Israel, who has sent you this day to meet me!

7894.label: 1 Samuel 25:33
7894.text: And blessed be your sensibleness, and blessed be you who have restrained me this day from entering into bloodguilt and having my own hand come to my salvation.

7895.label: 1 Samuel 25:34
7895.text: And, on the other hand, as Jehovah the God of Israel is living, who has held me back from doing injury to you, if you had not hastened that you might come to meet me, there would certainly not have remained to Naʹbal until the morning light anyone urinating against a wall.”

7896.label: 1 Samuel 25:35
7896.text: With that David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and to her he said: “Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice that I may have consideration for your person.”

7897.label: 1 Samuel 25:36
7897.text: Later Abʹi·gail came in to Naʹbal, and there he was having a feast in his house like the feast of the king; and Naʹbal’s heart was feeling good within him, and he was as drunk as could be; and she did not tell him a thing, small or great, until the morning light.

7898.label: 1 Samuel 25:37
7898.text: And it came about in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Naʹbal, that his wife went telling him these things. And his heart came to be dead inside him, and he himself became as a stone.

7899.label: 1 Samuel 25:38
7899.text: After that about ten days elapsed and then Jehovah struck Naʹbal, so that he died.

7900.label: 1 Samuel 25:39
7900.text: And David got to hear that Naʹbal had died, and so he said: “Blessed be Jehovah, who has conducted the legal case of my reproach [to free me] from Naʹbal’s hand and has kept his servant back from badness, and the badness of Naʹbal Jehovah has turned back upon his own head!” And David proceeded to send and propose to Abʹi·gail to take her as his wife.

7901.label: 1 Samuel 25:40
7901.text: So David’s servants came to Abʹi·gail at Carʹmel and spoke to her, saying: “David himself has sent us to you to take you as his wife.”

7902.label: 1 Samuel 25:41
7902.text: Immediately she rose up and bowed with her face to the earth and said: “Here is your slave girl as a maidservant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.”

7903.label: 1 Samuel 25:42
7903.text: Then Abʹi·gail hastened and rose up and went riding on the ass with five maids of hers walking behind her; and she went accompanying the messengers of David and then became his wife.

7904.label: 1 Samuel 25:43
7904.text: David had also taken A·hinʹo·am from Jezʹre·el; and the women came to be, even both of them, his wives.

7905.label: 1 Samuel 25:44
7905.text: As for Saul, he had given Miʹchal his daughter, David’s wife, to Palʹti the son of Laʹish, who was from Galʹlim.

7906.label: 1 Samuel 26:1
7906.text: In time the men of Ziph came to Saul at Gibʹe·ah, saying: “Is not David concealing himself on the hill of Hach·iʹlah, facing Je·shiʹmon?”

7907.label: 1 Samuel 26:2
7907.text: And Saul proceeded to rise up and go down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand men, the chosen ones of Israel, to look for David in the wilderness of Ziph.

7908.label: 1 Samuel 26:3
7908.text: And Saul took up camping on the hill of Hach·iʹlah, which faces Je·shiʹmon, by the road, while David was dwelling in the wilderness. And he got to see that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.

7909.label: 1 Samuel 26:4
7909.text: So David sent spies that he might know that Saul had for a fact come.

7910.label: 1 Samuel 26:5
7910.text: Later David rose up and went to the place where Saul had encamped, and David got to see the place where Saul had lain down, and also Abʹner the son of Ner the chief of his army; and Saul was lying in the camp enclosure with the people camping all around him.

7911.label: 1 Samuel 26:6
7911.text: Then David answered and said to A·himʹe·lech the Hitʹtite and A·bishʹai the son of Ze·ruʹiah, the brother of Joʹab: “Who will go down with me to Saul into the camp?” To this A·bishʹai said: “I myself shall go down with you.”

7912.label: 1 Samuel 26:7
7912.text: And David made his way with A·bishʹai to the people by night; and, look! Saul was lying asleep in the camp enclosure with his spear stuck into the earth at his head, and Abʹner and the people were lying all around him.

7913.label: 1 Samuel 26:8
7913.text: A·bishʹai now said to David: “God has today surrendered your enemy into your hand. And now let me, please, pin him to the earth with the spear just once, and I shall not do it to him twice.”

7914.label: 1 Samuel 26:9
7914.text: However, David said to A·bishʹai: “Do not bring him to ruin, for who is it that has thrust his hand out against the anointed of Jehovah and has remained innocent?”

7915.label: 1 Samuel 26:10
7915.text: And David went on to say: “As Jehovah is living, Jehovah himself will deal him a blow; or his day will come and he will have to die, or down into battle he will go, and he will certainly be swept away.

7916.label: 1 Samuel 26:11
7916.text: It is unthinkable, on my part, from Jehovah’s standpoint, to thrust my hand out against the anointed of Jehovah! So now take, please, the spear that is at his head and the water jug, and let us get on our way.”

7917.label: 1 Samuel 26:12
7917.text: Accordingly David took the spear and the water jug from the place at Saul’s head, and then they got on their way; and there was no one seeing nor anyone taking note nor anyone waking up, for all of them were asleep, because it was a deep sleep from Jehovah that had fallen upon them.

7918.label: 1 Samuel 26:13
7918.text: Then David passed on to the other side and stood upon the top of the mountain at a distance, the space between them being vast.

7919.label: 1 Samuel 26:14
7919.text: And David began to call out to the people and to Abʹner the son of Ner, saying: “Will you not answer, Abʹner?” And Abʹner began to answer and say: “Who are you that have called out to the king?”

7920.label: 1 Samuel 26:15
7920.text: And David went on to say to Abʹner: “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why, then, did you not watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to bring the king your lord to ruin.

7921.label: 1 Samuel 26:16
7921.text: This thing that you have done is not good. As Jehovah is living, YOU men deserve to die, because YOU have not watched over YOUR lord, over the anointed of Jehovah. And now see where the king’s spear and the water jug are that were at his head.”

7922.label: 1 Samuel 26:17
7922.text: And Saul began to recognize the voice of David and to say: “Is this your voice, my son David?” To this David said: “It is my voice, my lord the king.”

7923.label: 1 Samuel 26:18
7923.text: And he added: “Why is this that my lord is chasing after his servant, for what have I done, and what badness is there in my hand?

7924.label: 1 Samuel 26:19
7924.text: And now let my lord the king, please, listen to the words of his servant: If it is Jehovah that has incited you against me, let him smell a grain offering. But if it is the sons of man, they are cursed before Jehovah, because they have driven me out today from feeling myself attached to the inheritance of Jehovah, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods!’

7925.label: 1 Samuel 26:20
7925.text: And now do not let my blood fall to the earth before the face of Jehovah; for the king of Israel has gone out to look for a single flea, just as one chases a partridge upon the mountains.”

7926.label: 1 Samuel 26:21
7926.text: In turn Saul said: “I have sinned. Come back, my son David, for I shall no more do you injury, in view of the fact that my soul has been precious in your eyes this day. Look! I have acted foolishly and am very much mistaken.”

7927.label: 1 Samuel 26:22
7927.text: Then David answered and said: “Here is the spear of the king, and let one of the young men come on over and fetch it.

7928.label: 1 Samuel 26:23
7928.text: And Jehovah it is who will repay to each one his own righteousness and his own faithfulness, in that Jehovah today gave you into my hand, and I was unwilling to thrust my hand out against the anointed of Jehovah.

7929.label: 1 Samuel 26:24
7929.text: And, look! just as your soul was great this day in my eyes, so may my soul be great in the eyes of Jehovah, that he may deliver me out of all distress.”

7930.label: 1 Samuel 26:25
7930.text: At this Saul said to David: “Blessed may you be, my son David. Not only will you without fail work but you will also without fail come off the winner.” And David proceeded to go on his way; and as for Saul, he returned to his place.

7931.label: 1 Samuel 27:1
7931.text: However, David said in his heart: “Now I shall be swept away one day by Saul’s hand. There is nothing better for me than that I should escape without fail to the land of the Phi·lisʹtines; and Saul must despair of me in looking for me any longer in all the territory of Israel, and I shall certainly escape from his hand.”

7932.label: 1 Samuel 27:2
7932.text: So David rose up and he and six hundred men that were with him passed over to Aʹchish the son of Maʹoch, the king of Gath.

7933.label: 1 Samuel 27:3
7933.text: And David continued to dwell with Aʹchish in Gath, he and his men, each one with his household, David and his two wives, A·hinʹo·am the Jezʹre·el·i·tess and Abʹi·gail, Naʹbal’s wife, the Carʹmel·it·ess.

7934.label: 1 Samuel 27:4
7934.text: In time report was made to Saul that David had run away to Gath, and so he did not go looking for him still another time.

7935.label: 1 Samuel 27:5
7935.text: Then David said to Aʹchish: “If, now, I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities of the countryside, that I may dwell there; for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?”

7936.label: 1 Samuel 27:6
7936.text: Accordingly Aʹchish gave him Zikʹlag on that day. That is why Zikʹlag has come to belong to the kings of Judah down to this day.

7937.label: 1 Samuel 27:7
7937.text: And the number of the days that David dwelt in the countryside of the Phi·lisʹtines came to be a year and four months.

7938.label: 1 Samuel 27:8
7938.text: And David proceeded to go up with his men that they might raid the Geshʹur·ites and the Girʹzites and the A·malʹek·ites; for they were inhabiting the land that [extended] from Teʹlam as far as Shur and down to the land of Egypt.

7939.label: 1 Samuel 27:9
7939.text: And David struck the land, but he preserved neither man nor woman alive; and he took flocks and herds and asses and camels and garments, after which he returned and came to Aʹchish.

7940.label: 1 Samuel 27:10
7940.text: Then Aʹchish said: “Where did YOU men make a raid today?” To this David said: “Upon the south of Judah and upon the south of the Je·rahʹme·el·ites and upon the south of the Kenʹites.”

7941.label: 1 Samuel 27:11
